  "2023-12-19 00:00:00" "2023-12-19 06:00:00" --tag ztie-n1219 --dry-run` exits 1 with "ValueError: mask found_by must
  be one of ('time', 'polar', 'cluster', 'night', 'gate'), not 'dive'"; the same with `--no-masks` exits 0 [measured].
  207 of the 209 Z rows resolved; the two that failed are P3S6's.
- **Where:** `src/mt_workbench/masks.py`, `FOUND_BY` (line 123) and the check at lines 252-253. The survey's
  `surveys/MT_Morocco_Nador_Geothermal/masks.yaml` (declared 5 Oct 2026 on the logger-9 dive's proposal) gives P3S6's
  20 Dec 02:00-03:00 UTC entry `found_by: dive`, an origin the reader does not know.
- **Effect:** every aurora run that loads masks for P3S6, as the local or the remote, stops before processing. P3S6 is
  one of the nine forced E-tie sites. The inter-site estimator applies no masks, so the M products are not touched
  [inference from the M stage's README: "the inter-site estimator applies no masks"].

  sweep in the dive), or `FOUND_BY` gains `dive` (and `--mask-origins` with it). A validation of masks.yaml at the time
  a site's entry is written would have caught it.
- **See also:** `workbench_issues.md` 22, the same defect found by the Stacks tab's data map, which adds that the
  error names neither the site nor the entry and that the Stacks tab's availability chart catches it per site.
- **Update (2026-10-11):** The author declared the Nador entry `found_by: time` (masks.yaml edited; the reason line records it). P3S6's masked Z rows now run (study D3, `2026_Morocco_Nador_Geothermal/results/p3s6_mask_20261011/`). `FOUND_BY` still refuses `dive`, and the error still names neither the site nor the entry; the issue stays open for those two points.

## 73. mt-workbench (`ingest._ingest_bursts`): a recording whose last .td_24k file ends inside a burst cannot be ingested (2026-10-05)
- **Found:** the Kalkaroo P-test ingest (`2026_Natural_Source_IP/datasets/kalkaroo/results/ptest_20261005/`,
  `logs/ingest_PT_10306H_failed_cut_burst.log`). PT_10306H (logger 10306, MTU-5C) stops after 245 s with
  "ValueError: 10306_5FA258AB_0_00000088.td_24k: mt-io read 6 bursts of [48000, 48000, 48000]... samples, the
  sub-headers give 5 of [48000, 48000, 48000]...". The last file of every channel folder is 1,056,320 bytes and ends
  24000 samples into its sixth burst [measured]. 11 of the 12 P-test recordings end on a whole burst [measured].
- **Where:** `src/mt_workbench/ingest.py` `_ingest_bursts` (about line 2343) compares the sizes of every burst
  `_read_bursts` returns (mt-io's `DecimatedSegmentCollection`, which returns the cut burst with the samples the
  file holds) with `phoenix.burst_index`, which leaves a cut burst out with a warning. The check is per file, so a
  window that leaves only the cut burst out still fails while any slot uses that file.
- **Effect:** the whole site fails, after the burst archive has been written up to that file. Called through the
  library (the only route, entry 72) the partial archive stays on disk under the site's name (1.30 GB here). A
  recording stopped during a burst hits this: 2 s of every 30 s in 2020, so roughly one stop in 15 [inference].
- **Workaround:** `ingest_site(survey, "PT_10306H", end="2020-11-04T21:00:42")`, the first burst of the last file,
  which leaves out that file's 5 whole bursts and the cut one (1620 of 1625 bursts; `scripts/05b_ingest_burst.py`,
  criteria.txt amendment 6). The partial archive was renamed `PT_10306H.h5.partial_failed_20261005`.
- **Fix (not made here):** compare only the bursts the walk keeps (drop mt-io's trailing burst when its size is the
  walk's cut size), and remove the partial archive on any failure inside `_ingest_bursts`.
- **Fixed (7 Oct 2026):** `_ingest_bursts` drops mt-io's trailing burst when the file holds one more burst than the
  walk and that burst's size is `phoenix.cut_burst_samples` (the samples after the cut burst's sub-header), and removes
  the archive it was writing on any failure (`_remove_partial_archive`). Tests: tests/ingest_phoenix_unit.py U13 (G5
  with its second .td_24k file cut 24000 samples into its last burst: 23 runs equal to the walk, the warning; a failure
  forced after five runs leaves no file; both failed on ca0dc53, two mutations trip). Real data: PT_10306H through
  ingest_site.py into the scratch workspace, 1625 runs in 565 s; its first 1620 runs equal the P-test workaround's
  (start, end, four channels sample for sample), the other 5 the last file's whole bursts, the cut burst (24000
  samples) in no run; a failure forced after 50 runs left nothing.

## 74. mt-workbench (`phoenix.archive_stamp_correction`): 206 s on a burst archive of 1629 runs (2026-10-05)
- **Found:** the P-test archive checks (`ptest_20261005/scripts/06_check_archives.py`, logs/06_*): 201-233 s per
  burst archive of 1625-1649 runs, against under 1 s for a 150 Hz archive of one run [measured]. A profile of PT_10133H:
  the sub-header walk of 544 files 1.6 s, an h5py read of every run's and channel's comments 2.3 s,
  `archive_stamp_correction` 206 s [measured].
- **Where:** `src/mt_workbench/phoenix.py` `archive_stamp_correction` opens the archive with mth5 and calls
  `get_station(...).metadata`, which builds the metadata of every run of the station to read one attribute.
- **Effect:** `scripts/merge_tensor_bands.py` calls it for each of the six archives of a stitch, so a stitch of
  whole-recording burst sites spends about 10 min reading three comments [inference: 3 x 206 s].
- **Fix (not made here):** read the station group's `provenance.comments` attribute with h5py, as
  `dclevel.recorded_levels` reads run comments.
- **Fixed (7 Oct 2026):** `archive_stamp_correction` reads the station group's `provenance.comments` attribute with
  h5py (read-only, no file lock) and raises `MTH5Error` for a missing archive or station as before. PT_10133H.h5 (1629
  runs): 1.0 in 0.002 s, against 1.0 in 106 s with ca0dc53 measured the same evening; the 12 P-test burst archives
  all 1.0 in 1-2 ms. Test: tests/phoenix_archive_unit.py (values equal to the mth5 read on six fixtures and

## 75. mt_metadata 1.0.10: a `Comment` value holding "|" is split into time stamp, author and value, also when set through `.comments.value` (2026-10-05)
- **Found:** the Stacks tab's recipe provenance (`virtual.build_synthetic_remote(provenance=)`), a JSON line in
  a stack archive's run comment. A value of two lines, `line one` and `provenance: {"a":1,"b":"x|y"}`, set with
  `run.metadata.comments.value = ...` and written with `write_metadata()` is stored as two attributes,
  `comments.author` = everything before the "|" and `comments.value` = `'y"}'`, and mt_metadata logs an ERROR
  from `mttime._parse_string` while it tries the first piece as a time [measured, scratch MTH5].
- **Where:** `mt_metadata/common/comment.py` `Comment.set_variables` (lines 91-110), a `model_validator(mode="after")`
  that splits any value holding "|" and keeps only the last piece as the value. The metadata models validate on
  assignment (`base/metadata.py` line 327, `validate_assignment=True`), so setting `.value` runs it too; the
  mt-workbench comment that `.comments.value` avoids the parse (virtual.py, the weights comments) holds only for
  text without "|".
- **Effect:** free text with a "|" in any comment (a JSON value, a YAML block scalar, a note quoting a command line
  with a pipe) loses everything before the last "|" on write. Nothing is raised; the ERROR line names a time parse.
- **Workaround in mt-workbench:** `virtual._provenance_line` writes every "|" of the JSON as its JSON escape
  (backslash u007c), which `json.loads` reads back as "|"; a recipe name or hash holding "|" is refused.
- **Ask upstream:** split on "|" only when parsing the "time | author | value" string form (`from_dict`, reading
  a file), never when a value is assigned, or offer a field that keeps the text as given.

## 76. mt-workbench (`phoenix.recording_files`): a 0-byte `.td_150` file stops a Phoenix ingest (2026-10-08)
- **Found:** the Kalkaroo S1 ingest (`2026_Natural_Source_IP/datasets/kalkaroo/runs/ingest_S1_20261007/`,
  `logs/ingest/J12.log`, ledger exit 1). J12 (receiver 10240, MTU-5C) stops after 3.5 s with "ValueError: J12:
  10240_5FAB0A04_0_00000108.td_150: 0 bytes, shorter than the 128-byte header". The last `.td_150` of each of the
  four channel folders, sequence 0x108, is 0 bytes; the other 263 per folder are whole (one of 215,528 bytes, 262 of
  216,128) [measured]. KD-G5 (receiver 10242, S3) has the same: `10242_608B9983_*_0000009D.td_150` is a trailing
  0-byte file in channel folders 0 and 4 and missing in folders 1 and 2, which end at 0x9C (156 whole files in each
  folder); 8a72107 refuses the site with "10242_608B9983_0_0000009D.td_150: 0 bytes, shorter than the 128-byte
  header", the fix plans it as one run of sequences 1-156 [measured: the sceptic's plan comparison over raw_sites,
  `ingest_gaps_fix_20261007/sceptic/logs/plans_compare.log`, and the file sizes].
- **Where:** `src/mt_workbench/phoenix.py` `recording_files` reads every file's header
  (`instruments.phoenix_header`), which raises on a file shorter than its 128-byte header; `ingest._phoenix_units`
  raises it again with the site's name.
- **Effect:** a whole site is refused for a file that holds no sample. J12's 263 files (26.3 h) have no archive,
  and with it 2 of the 126 adjacent S1 pairs (K12-J12, J12-H12).
- **Workaround:** none in the code; moving the empty files out of the extracted folder would change the raw record.
- **Fix:** skip a file of no more than its header with a warning naming it. A trailing one then ends the recording;
  one in the middle of a folder leaves its sequence missing there, which entry 77 handles.
- **Fixed (8 Oct 2026):** `recording_files` skips a file of no more than its 128-byte header with a warning naming
  it ("10240_5FAB0A04_0_00000108.td_150: 0 bytes, no sample past the 128-byte header: skipped"), and refuses a
  folder whose every file of the type is empty (the channel would vanish). Tests: tests/phoenix_files_unit.py (a
  trailing 0-byte sequence in every folder: one run, four warnings) and tests/ingest_phoenix_unit.py U15 (G5Z, a cut
  of the real G5 with a 0-byte sequence 4 in every folder: one run of files 1-3, each channel equal to its folder's
  files, four warnings); both failed on 8a72107. Real data: J12 through scripts/ingest_site.py into
  `D:/MT_DATA/MT_Kalkaroo_Workspace/mth5/scratch_gaps_fix`: one run, files 1-263, 14,201,850 samples per channel
  (53,850 + 262 x 54,000), every channel equal to its folder's 263 files, first sample 2020-11-10 21:45:23.8852 UTC,
  the four empty files named.

## 77. mt-workbench (`phoenix.plan_runs`): a sequence missing from one channel folder stops a Phoenix ingest (2026-10-08)
- **Found:** the same ingest, `logs/ingest/E10.log`. E10 (receiver 10135, MTU-8A) stops with "ValueError: E10:
  10135_5FAB2337_3_0000000E.td_150: the channel folders do not hold the same files (sequence numbers and sample
  counts) as folder 0". Channel folder 3 (H1, hx) holds 478 files and lacks sequence 0x0D
  (10135_5FAB2337_3_0000000D.td_150, the 13th of 479); folders 0, 2 and 7 hold all 479 [measured]. The message
  names 0x0E, the first file of folder 3 that differs from folder 0 at the same position, not the missing one.
- **Where:** `plan_runs` refuses any recording whose channel folders differ in sequence numbers or sample counts.
- **Effect:** E10's 479 files (47.8 h) are refused for 360 s missing in one channel; 2 more of the 126 pairs
  (E10-E9, E10-E11) have no product, and the NE corner's storm night of 10-11 Nov loses the site.
- **Workaround:** none in the code.
- **Fix:** keep the sequences that every folder holds with one sample count. A sequence that some folder lacks
  (absent, empty, or with another count) is left out of every channel and becomes a run boundary: the run before
  ends at the last whole sequence, the run after starts at the next sequence every folder holds, the seconds left
  out are logged and written into the run comment, and nothing is interpolated. A recording whose folders agree
  gives the runs it gave before.
- **Fixed (8 Oct 2026):** `plan_runs` aligns the folders first (`phoenix._aligned_files`): a sequence some folder
  lacks, holds empty or holds with another sample count is left out of every channel, the existing time check then
  splits the run there, and `_gap_notes` logs the gap and puts a line on the run after it (`RunPlan.notes`, added to
  the run comment by `read_continuous`), e.g. "phoenix_gap: sequence 13 (not in folder 3) left out of every channel,
  360 s from the end of sequence 12 to the start of sequence 14". Tests: tests/phoenix_files_unit.py (sequence 2
  missing, empty or 60 s short in one folder: runs 1 and 3-4 in every folder, the note; each folder's own files is
  the mutation) and tests/ingest_phoenix_unit.py U15 (G5M, G5E: two runs, each channel equal to its own folder's
  files, run 2 at sequence 3's time in every channel to the ns, the line) and U16 (the 25 recordings of the test
  folder plan as the stored 8a72107 fixture); U15 failed on 8a72107. Real data: E10 into the scratch workspace, two
  runs, files 1-12 (647,850 samples per channel) and 14-479 (25,119,000), every channel equal to its folder's files,
  run 2 starting in every channel 360.006667 s (360 s and one sample) after run 1's last sample, the line in run 2's
  comment; the 141 other recordings under raw_sites (S1 and the P-test) plan exactly as on 8a72107, so their
  archives would be rebuilt the same. The missing file is sequence 0x0D (10135_5FAB2337_3_0000000D.td_150), not
  0x0E, which the old message named.

## 78. mt-workbench (`dclevel.rail_fraction`): the "saturated?" flag of a Phoenix run counts electrode drift (2026-10-08)
- **Found:** the S1 archive QC (`2026_Natural_Source_IP/datasets/kalkaroo/results/s1_qc_20261007/README.md`,
  finding 2 and Q4; `sceptic/independent/README.md` check 1). The ingest flagged 140 channel runs at 76 S1 sites
  "saturated?" (all E: 71 ex, 69 ey). No channel run has more than 0.0041 % of its 150 Hz samples at the ADC rail,
  0.9 x the input range (5 V / the header's total circuitry gain: 2.25 V for E at gain 2, 1.125 V for H at gain 4);
  the flagged runs peak at 2.1-46 mV. The flag reproduces exactly (140 of 140 recomputed with `channel_stats`).
- **Where:** `src/mt_workbench/dclevel.py` `rail_fraction` puts a sample at the rail when it lies beyond 0.9 of the
  record's own largest excursion from the median; `ingest._run_levels` and `ingest._ingest_bursts` measure Phoenix
  runs with it.
- **Effect:** a channel whose median drifts a few mV over a run puts up to 100 % of an hour's samples "at the
  rail"; ingest_site.py's flag lines and the Metadata tab's dc level column show saturation where there is none.
- **Workaround:** read none of the Phoenix "saturated?" flags as saturation (the QC's proposal 3).
- **Fix:** for a Phoenix run the rail is absolute, RAIL_LEVEL (0.9) x each channel's input range from its file
  header (mt-io's `Header.ad_plus_minus_range / total_circuitry_gain`, the range mt-io's `NativeReader` scales input
  volts by), recorded in the run comment and named in the flag line; LEMI and EDL runs keep the relative rail. The
  receiver's saturated-frame counts are not used: the `.td_150` headers hold 2,185 of the 5,641 frames the stats
  files record inside the storm windows (QC finding 3), mt-io decodes the header count wrongly (entry 79), the
  ingest does not read the stats files, and a frame count describes the 24 kHz converter, not the stored samples.
- **Fixed (8 Oct 2026):** `dclevel.channel_stats(..., rail=)` and `rail_fraction(..., rail=)` count |x| >= rail;
  `ingest._phoenix_rails` gives each channel 0.9 x `phoenix.input_range_v` of its first file (following hx and hy
  through swap_h), passed for continuous runs (`_run_levels`) and bursts (`_ingest_bursts`); `level_note` adds
  "dc rail (V, 0.9 x the input range): ex 2.25, ..." after the levels, `parse_level_note` reads it back, and
  `flag_line` names it ("3.00 % at the input rail (|x| >= 2.25 V), saturated?"). LEMI and EDL calls pass no rail and
  keep their lines. Tests: tests/dc_level_unit.py (a drifting E 21.95 % at its own rail, 0.00 % at 2.25 V; a
  railed E 1.51 % and 3.00 %, flagged in both; rail ignored is the mutation; failed on 8a72107) and
  tests/ingest_phoenix_unit.py U17 (the G5 cuts' run comments give back 2.25 V for E and 1.125 V for H). Real data:
  C10, E6 and K5 of S1 re-measured from their archives (read only): 6 flags recorded, as the QC; 0 with the rail;
  the share over all samples equals the QC's rail_by_site.csv for all 12 channel runs (E6 hy 0.00415 %, 0.00398 %
  on the ingest's subsample); J12 and E10 ingested with every channel run ok. The 140 flags already recorded in the
  S1 archives stay until those sites are ingested again. scripts/dc_level_check.py (at the sceptic's word, 8 Oct)
  measured every archive against the record's own rail, so it reported the sceptic's rebuilt C10 "saturated?" (ex
  9.49 %, ey 11.62 %) while the run comment records 0.00 % ok; it now reads the rail back from the run comment
  (`comment_rails`, through `parse_level_note`) and measures a channel the comment names a rail for against it, any
  other against the record's own rail as before (C10: 0.00 % in all four channels, none flagged; the CSV gains
  `rail_level`). Test: tests/dc_level_unit.py (a 150 Hz run whose comment carries the rail line and a control run
  without it; the comment's rail not read is the mutation).

## 79. mt-io 0.0.5: `Header.saturated_frames` decodes the raw count 1,480 as 1,152 (2026-10-08)
- **Found:** the S1 QC's sceptic (`s1_qc_20261007/sceptic/independent/README.md`, check 1b). Of 10,500
  channel-hours, one `.td_150` header count differs between a raw read of the uint16 at offset 101 and mt-io's
  `Header`: E6 hy, 12 Nov 2020 04:00 UTC, raw 1,480, mt-io 1,152. The receiver's stats files give 1,480 for that
  hour [measured by the QC and its sceptic].
- **Where:** `mt_io/phoenix/readers/header.py` `Header.saturated_frames`: when bit 0x80 of the uint16 is set it keeps
  the low 7 bits and shifts them left by 4 (1,480 = 0x5C8 has bit 7 set; 0x48 << 4 = 1,152).
- **Effect:** every count with bit 7 set (128-255, 384-511, ..., 1,408-1,535) is replaced by another number, so
  anything that counts frames through mt-io miscounts large events. mt-workbench does not read the field.
- **Workaround:** read the uint16 at header offset 101 raw (`struct.unpack_from("<H", header, 101)`), as the QC did.
  The `.td_150` header counts hold only part of the saturation the receiver's stats files record (2,185 of 5,641
  frames inside the S1 storm windows, 1,484 of 3,704 outside), so a saturation mask is built on the stats files.
- **Ask upstream:** decode the uint16 as stored, or name the format the 0x80 rule belongs to.

## 80. mt-workbench (`instruments.record_files`): a 0-byte Phoenix file stops the raw-file listing (2026-10-08)
- **Found:** while fixing entry 76 (8 Oct 2026). `record_files(raw_sites/J12, "phoenix")` raises "ValueError:
  10240_5FAB0A04_0_00000108.td_150: 0 bytes, shorter than the 128-byte header" [measured], and KD-G5's stops on

- **Effect:** scripts/new_survey.py on a folder holding J12 or KD-G5 stops; the GUI's window bar
