## 356. aurora fork 0.6.2+mtproc (`aurora.pipelines.transfer_function_helpers.window_mask_for_band`): a band the window masks would empty is processed unmasked, on every window, with a log warning only, so a masked product silently holds whole-record bands; at 1 Hz the bands over 16,384 s rest on 6-18 six-day STFT windows and a day selection empties most of them (2026-10-23)
- **Found:** Tasmania AusLAMP 2016 stage 5 (agent L, 23 Oct 2026 15:2x-15:3x WAST), the long-end day selections (`<ws>\qc\stage5\s2_windows.csv`, `s2_mask_acted.csv`, from the runs' logs `<ws>\qc\stage5\logs
uns\s2_*.log`): TAS100L rr TAS107L, band masks [3000, 1e6] s over the 40 % of days left out; level 6 (18,390-58,386 s) holds 8 STFT windows of 524,288 s over the 24-day overlap; every random 60 % draw would have left 0 of 8, and aurora logged "window masks would leave band 58385.938392s 0 of 8 STFT windows (minimum 1): band left unmasked" for each of the six bands and estimated them on all 8 windows; the coherent-day selection kept 1 of 8 (then not written: min_band_windows 2) and the quiet-day selection 3 of 8. Over the six sites, in the 10,000-90,000 s verdict window the median random draw had 6 of 8 bands left unmasked.
- **Where:** the projects folderurora (installed 0.6.2+mtproc), `window_mask_for_band`: `if t.size - int(drop.sum()) < minimum: ... return None` (minimum = max(1, stft.min_num_stft_windows)); mt_workbench's patch path (`process._band_masks_applied`, MIN_MASKED_WINDOWS 4) skips a mask the same way and records it in `_BandMaskLog`, but the fork path records nothing the sidecar sees.

A selection experiment's random control then equals the whole record in those bands, so a control "beats" or "loses" by construction; any masked long-period product can carry unmasked bands without a trace outside the log.
- **Workaround:** stage 5 reads the log lines (`s2_eval.window_counts`) and reports per job the share of the window's bands in which the mask acted; the long-end selections were judged void where it did not.
- **Ask:** a choice on the config for a band the masks would empty: drop the band (not estimated, so the period is not written) or keep it unmasked, the default being to drop it; and in either case the band's record (windows, kept, skipped) returned with the TF so that process_rr.py can write it in the sidecar (mt-workbench issue 57). A test: a mask over the whole record of one level drops that level's bands (or records the skip), never estimates them unmasked unrecorded.

Skipping this decimation level."

## 359. ## 360. WA-MT campaign code (`WAMT_Campaign_2026-10\code\copy_test_timedomain.py`, the campaign copy of the author's `wamt_copy_test.py`): on a cache-DEAD line the test reads the cache's assembled line, which is NaN end to end, so its day loop skips every day and it returns "CLEAN (0 of 0 days with R2 > 0.5)", a verdict it cannot fail to give; in the other direction `hp` turns the NaN line into zeros and the live line regressed on zeros reads "CLEAN (0 of N days)" (2026-10-23)
- **Found:** murchison_oct2024 finish part 1 (23 Oct 17:42:57-17:43:24 WAST), the copy test as it is on the campaign cache at the six sites with a dead-labelled line [measured: Murchison_Oct2024\finish\copy_test_registered.csv]: MBP19 Ex, MBK23 Ex and Ey, MBI21 Ex and Ey, MBJ21 Ey, MBK21 Ex, MBN20 Ey each "CLEAN (0 of 0 days ...)"; the live lines regressed on them "CLEAN (0 of 22-44 days ...)". The same rows stand in batch 1's logs\batch1_fixround\copy_test_esperance2.csv at MBS23 Ey and MBS24 Ey.
- **Where:** `main`'s day loop (`if not np.isfinite(yy).all() or np.var(yy) == 0: continue`) on `W.rotated(site)`'s `loc["Ex"]` / `loc["Ey"]`; `hp` (`np.nan_to_num`) for the regressor. The products of such a line are not made from NaN: wamt_run.fill_dead_lines (wamt_halves.dead_fill) fills it with the plain mean of its own two stored arms before any pass.
- **Effect:** a dead-labelled line's copy_test flag would read CLEAN without a single day read (rulings_campaign_fulldelivery_addendum2 3 makes the word a delivered flag); a gate that only asks "was the test run on the line" passes it.
- **Workaround:** this finish runs the script unchanged on a scratch cache whose all-NaN lines carry the runner's fill (code\scratchpad\finish\copytest_cache_m24.py; Murchison_Oct2024\finish\copytest\fill\): every dead line read on 22-45 days: MBP19 Ex NO FIELD, MBK23 Ex COPY REMOVABLE, MBK23 Ey MIXED, MBI21 Ex COPY REMOVABLE, MBI21 Ey NO FIELD, MBJ21 Ey CLEAN, MBK21 Ex GEOLOGY, MBN20 Ey CLEAN (COPY_TEST_timedomain.csv); its control (MBO19 Ey := 0.5 Ex + 0.05 Ey) COPY REMOVABLE at a +0.507. Batch 1's MBS23 Ey and MBS24 Ey words were never measured on their lines.
- **Ask:** in the copy test, take a cache-DEAD line as the runner takes it (the mean of its stored arms, named in the row), and write "NOT READ (0 days)" rather than CLEAN where no day is read.

## 362. MTH5_Aurora_mt-io_2026 (the cross cache's H at a quarter-turned fluxgate: `wamt_murchison_prep`'s reversed-fluxgate flip, upstream 300, then `wamt_remotes.rot_h`'s mean-field angle), seen in the products: at murchison_oct2024's MBP26 every one of the ten impedance products (5 kinds x 2 policies) has both off-diagonals in the opposite quadrant at every period of 30-3,000 s (Zxy median -140 to -142 deg, Zyx +39 deg), the kinds agreeing with each other, so 9.11.1 refuses both components on the quadrant clause and the site has no product of record (2026-10-23)
- **Found:** murchison_oct2024 finish part 1 (23 Oct 17:39-17:5x WAST) [measured: Murchison_Oct2024\READINGS.csv, PRODUCTS_OF_RECORD_whole.csv; this stage's own EDI reader on the ten pass files]: every candidate's worst-decade corroborated fraction 0.000 in every decade at xy and yx while the cross-kind leg agrees at 36-40 of 40 judged points; over the 21 periods of 30-3,000 s the in-quadrant fraction is 0.00 and the opposite-quadrant fraction 1.00 for Zxy and Zyx in all ten products (the single station too). - **Where:** the H of the cache: h_sign -1 from the mean raw Hx of -96.8 nT (the cross builder's reversed-fluxgate test; upstream 300: "ill-posed near a zero mean"), the regime's one whole-record rot_h angle -89.7817 deg; the product's INFO reads "h_rotation_deg=0.0-end d: -89.782" and "frame=H in the mean horizontal field frame, E in the instrument frame". A sign error of H (or of both E lines) against the other negates Z, which is what is seen; which of the two (the flip, the angle's sense at a near-90 deg frame, or the E wiring of the turned logger) is not settled by the products and is not this stage's (rulings_batch2 item 4 ruled H as cached with the quarter turn carried by rot_h; MBP26 has no release to compare).

- **Workaround:** none in this stage (Z is delivered as recorded); the reading, the numbers and the frame are in the finish's tables and report for the owner.
- **Ask:** decide MBP26's H sign at the cache from the variation frame against neighbours (the turn test of 19 Oct 14:13 read a pure rotation of about -88.5 deg against MBQ25 and MBQ24) rather than from the sign of a near-zero mean Hx, and write the decision with the measured angle into the cache's provenance; a check in the readings that flags a site whose every product sits in the opposite quadrant.

## 396. mth5 0.6.9 (`ChannelDataset._station_metadata_with`, every channel read of a burst station): the station metadata handed to each channel time series is built from the station group's attributes with the whole `run_list`, so a station of thousands of one-burst runs materialises every run for every channel read and the channel's constructor copies them all again (2026-10-28)
- **Found:** the Kalkaroo burst pilot's Z rows (results/burst_pilot_20261028, 28 Oct 2026): aurora's `initialize_dataframe_for_processing` took 31 s per burst run on G7H.h5 (2907 runs); py-spy on the live run showed the time in `copy.deepcopy` under `ChannelTS.__init__` -> `_validate_survey_metadata` -> `survey_metadata.copy()`, called from `ChannelDataset.time_slice` inside `RunGroup.to_runts`.
- **Where:** `mth5/groups/channel_dataset.py` `_station_metadata_with` (reads `dict(self.hdf5_dataset.parent.parent.attrs)`, whose `run_list` names every run, so `Station.from_dict` creates them all) and `_survey_metadata_with`; `_metadata_levels` is used by `time_slice` and `to_channel_ts`. `RunGroup.station_metadata` (`groups/run.py`) sets `meta_dict["run_list"] = [self.metadata.id]` first and costs 0.01 s. Measured on G7H.h5 [measured]: `run.station_metadata` 0.01 s (1 run); `channel._metadata_levels()` 2.32 s (2907 runs in the station); `survey_metadata.copy()` 1.65 s; `time_slice` of one channel 5.05 s; `to_runts` 30.8 s.
- **Effect:** a Z run through aurora on a burst archive spends about 31 s per burst run before any estimate (300 bursts: 2.6 h per site), and `check_if_fcs_already_exist` pays the same per run; the products are unaffected (the RunTS already carries the run group's one-run station metadata).
- **Workaround:** `mt_workbench.process.slim_station_metadata()` (28 Oct 2026, uncommitted while the working tree holds other work) replaces `_station_metadata_with` for one processing call with a version that sets `run_list` to the channel's run before `Station.from_dict`, as the run path does; `kernel_dataset` and `process_station` run inside it. tests/burst_station_metadata_unit.py.
- **Ask:** trim `run_list` to the current run in `_station_metadata_with` (one line, as `RunGroup.station_metadata` does), or build the station metadata once per run group and hand it to every channel.
- **Three more costs of the same run list, found by the probes of 22:18 WAST (results/burst_pilot_20261028/logs/zprobe*_G7H_10bursts.log, a 10-burst window on G7H against RR_201105H) [measured]:** (a) `KernelDataset.from_run_summary` builds metadata for every run of the summary before the workbench clips to the window (9 min for 6747 runs); (b) `KernelDataset.get_metadata_from_df` reads `StationGroup.survey_metadata` per station, whose getter opens every run group of the station (`StationGroup.metadata`, `groups/station.py` 296-312: 30 s for 2907 runs), and aurora's `check_if_fcs_already_exist` opens the station once per run (`mth5_has_fcs`, 3.3 s each); (c) the transfer function's station metadata carries every run of the station, so a 10-burst product wrote a 19.9 MB EDI and a 3.5 MB XML (2909 run blocks) and the XML writer took 5 min. Workarounds in `mt_workbench.process`: `_drop_runs_outside` clips the run summary before the kernel dataset; `slim_station_metadata(wanted)` fills only the window's runs in the station getter and answers the Fourier-coefficient question from the file when the station stores none; `_keep_processed_runs` keeps `transfer_function.runs_processed` in the product. Probe 1 (the channel path alone): 1182 s; probe 2 (with the run-summary clip): 563 s.

## 403. `scripts/merge_tensor_bands.py` overlap check: the merge refuses when any of 10 correlated cells (4 elements and arg(det)/2 at two shared bands) has |z| > 2 with jackknife sigmas, so it refuses 19-21 % of perfectly agreeing merges (2026-10-29, Kalkaroo burst S1, E1)
- **Found:** 29 Oct 14:20 WAST, E1 of results/burst_S1_20261029 (FAIL 94 of 126 non-storm merges exit 0, 101 needed); the false-refusal rate measured by its sceptic 21:5x-22:0x (results/burst_S1_20261029/README.md, section "Defects met"; skeptic/README.md section 2).
- **Where:** `scripts/merge_tensor_bands.py` lines 172-185 (the overlap check, "fails if any |z| > 2 in a shared band"); the sigmas from `mt_workbench.intersite._jackknife_sd`.
- **Effect:** a complex element's jackknife sigma is that of its modulus, so a calibrated cell exceeds 2 with P = exp(-4) = 0.0183, and psi with 0.0455; the max over 10 correlated cells refuses 21.4 % (independent cells) or 19.2 % (the halves' correlation) of perfectly agreeing merges, simulated from the 133 S1 products' own sigmas (skeptic/tables/s06_e1_power.csv). A gate of "80 % of merges exit 0" then sits at the expected pass count (99.0-101.8 of 126): a coin flip on perfect data. The refusals are not evidence of disagreement by themselves.
- **Workaround:** none in that study (no --accept-disagreement; E1 recorded as FAIL with the power numbers beside it); a gate computed from the CSVs per cell (as its MU2 does) for the next study.
- **Ask:** give the check a stated false-refusal rate: a per-cell limit for the number of cells (about 2.30 for an element, 2.81 for psi at a 5 % family rate over 10 cells), or a chi-square over the cells; say so in the script's criterion text; optionally take an error factor per band.

## 427. Inter-receiver timing of the Phoenix 24 kHz bursts is neither checked nor corrected: J08 (MTU-5C 10305) lags K9_repeat (10307) by 35-56 us and P3 (10246) by 11-36 us, channel-dependent; no gate reads timing_check and Filters/time_delay is empty (2026-10-30, Kalkaroo burst S5, sceptic)
- **Found:** 30 Oct 16:26-16:35 WAST, the sceptic of results/burst_S5_20261030 (skeptic/scripts/k06_timing.py, k05b_swings_coherent.py; skeptic/tables/k06_timing.csv, k05b_swings.csv; runlog.txt).
- **Where:** the burst T path of `scripts/process_intersite.py` (its timing_check block writes a tau per product and says when the phase is not a line in frequency, but nothing downstream reads it); the archives' Filters/time_delay (empty); the study's B1 "clock offset 0" clause, which reads metadata only.
- **Effect:** calibrated H-H and E-E cross-spectra between the archives over the 121 shared night-1 bursts (500-5000 Hz, coherent grid search, 10-group jackknife), independent of T: J08|K9_repeat hx 49.1 +- 6.5, hy 34.8 +- 9.7, ex 41.3, ey 56.4 us; J08|P3 hx 35.7, hy 11.2, ex 13.8, ey 35.5 us; K9_repeat|P3 hx -13.6 +- 2.0, hy -22.5 +- 4.9, ex -26.8, ey -17.2 us; H closure over the triangle within 1.2 us (ey 3.7). One sample at 24 kHz is 41.7 us. The lags predict the products' psi at 0.000236 s (-66.2, -36.9, +28.7 deg against -62.1, -37.3, +27.8) within 4.1 deg, so the study's R5 extremes there are timing, not ground. The T products' own timing_check agrees (+50.0 +- 3.6, +29.4 +- 5.7, -22.3 +- 0.3 us; J08|K9 xx 32.5, yy 62.8 us, chi2/dof 35.3: "not a clock offset alone"). At 300 m (S1, S2) the sidecar taus were within +-7 us, which can move the shortest band by up to about 11 deg [arithmetic].
- **Workaround:** psi below about 0.001 s is read as timing-borne until a timing reading exists; the study README quotes the coherent-band swings after the sceptic's timing (12.6-16.9 deg).
- **Ask:** a timing reading per pair (H-H cross-phase tau with its error) written beside every burst T product and read by a gate; once the source is known (per-channel phase not carried by the calibration is one candidate [inference]), a per-receiver, per-channel time_delay filter.

## 450. results/psi_atlas_dense_20261031 plan.txt S6a: the synthetic-truth criterion fails by chance in 89-96 % of realisations, because every site's z shares the gauge's noise (2026-10-31, Kalkaroo psi atlas, plan)
- **Found:** 31 Oct 18:3x WAST, the sceptic (scripts/sceptic.py S6a, S6a_spread; sceptic/tables/sceptic.csv).
- **Where:** plan.txt S6 (a): "FAILS unless z = (phi - phi_true) / phi_err over the sites has |median| < 0.2 and 0.8 < sd < 1.2, and chi2/dof lies within 1 +- 3 sqrt(2 / dof)", judged on one realisation.
- **Effect:** in the gauge form every site's error includes the gauge's own noise (mean pairwise z correlation 0.43 for S1, 0.27 for S2), so one realisation's median and sd over the sites swing widely: median z 5-95 % -1.20 to +1.12 (S1). The criterion failed on the run of record (S1 median z +0.676, sd 0.667; S2 -0.539, 1.048) and fails by chance in 96.0 % (S1) and 89.3 % (S2) of 300 realisations. The solve is right: per site over 300 realisations, mean z -0.166 to -0.005 (S1) and -0.074 to +0.095 (S2) against 3/sqrt(300) = 0.173, sd 0.90-1.08; halving the errors makes the per-site form fail (sd 1.32 / 2.21).
- **Workaround:** the study README reports S6a as FAIL with the reason; the check was not changed.
- **Ask:** none for the workbench; a stamped amendment by the main session (per-site z over N realisations, mean within 3/sqrt(N), sd 0.8-1.2). A synthetic control is run on its own ideal case before hashing, and judged on a statistic that does not share a common term across its samples.

## 477. MTH5_Aurora_mt-io_2026 processing code (the lent-H cache builder, `Murchison_Dec2024\code\scratchpad\passes\lent_cache_mbn9_dec24.py` / lent_cache_v2, with LENDER_MBN9.csv's shift_for on Hy): one clock lag is applied where the recovered site's Hy against the lender's Hy is period-dependent (2026-11-01)
- **Found:** the F7 skeptic of murchison_add's finish part 1 (1 Nov 01:46-01:51 WAST; ..\WAMT_Campaign_2026-10\logs\skeptic_batch4_finish\sk4f_mbn9_lag.csv, sk4f_mbn9_lag_bands.csv).
- **Where:** the lent cache v2 advances MBN8's H by one lag, +0.066 s. R20's provenance words quote it beside "the two bases MBN8 +0.36 s and MBN10 +0.09 s at 20-200 s".
- **Effect:**
  - MBN9's own Hy (WAMT_cache_1hz\MBN9.npz, the 13 Oct clock file) against MBN8's Hy, as per-day medians of the coherence-weighted cross-spectral phase slope over 38 days: +0.071 s at 10-20 s, +0.174 s at 20-50 s, +0.334 s at 50-200 s and -0.302 s at 200-1,000 s.
  - A clock offset is the same in every band. This is a phase difference of about 1.2-2.0 deg between the two sites' Hy, 41.5 km apart: the false-clock case (a period-dependent lag is a phase).
  - +0.066 s is the short-period value and +0.36 s the 20-200 s value of the same difference. Days 0, 18 and 19 at 20-200 s read +0.46, +0.81 and +0.69 s (the record: +0.56, +0.51, +0.41).

- **Workaround:** none; named in the skeptic's hand-back (FINDINGS S4).

The key names READINGS.csv's two-arm production row (`_runs_mask\aurora\gng_kaiser20_75\MBK08.edi`: 0.95033 / 0.772116), not the rebuild's file (`_runs_arms\mask\_runs_mask_rebuild_MBK08\aurora\gng_kaiser20_75\MBK08.edi`: the author's tip_mag on it gives 0.950199 / 0.773047). ## 488. mt_metadata 1.0.10 (`transfer_functions/io/emtfxml/emtfxml.py` `EMTFXML._parse_comments`, lines 762-815, reached from `TF.write(file_type="xml")` through `mt_workbench.products.write_xml`): a TF read back from a workbench EDI carries the whole INFO block in its station comments; the XML writer takes each `key: value` piece as an attribute path, fails on the run lines (`sr10_000N.<channel>.<field>`), logs "Cannot set attribute ..." and drops the piece, so the XML of a product built from EDIs loses its source's run and channel metadata, with about 300 warning lines per product (2026-11-01)
- **Found:** Tasmania stage 6, agent E1, writing the 60 remote-median products (`<ws>/qc/stage6/scripts/e_build.py`, 1 Nov 2026 08:04; `<ws>` = D:\MT_DATA\MT_Tasmania_AusLAMP_2016_Workspace). `<ws>/qc/stage6/e/logs/e_build.log` holds 18,845 "Cannot set attribute" warnings, 177 per key (sr10_0001-0003, ex ey hx hy hz, each field: `sr10_0003.hy.measurement_azimuth`, `sr10_0003.hz.h_field_max.end`, ...) [measured]. P's TF read from `tf/TAS100_rr-TAS126_20261023-0130_tasmania10-default.edi` holds a station comment of 15,865 characters with 318 `sr10_000` mentions (the INFO block) [measured]. The written `tf/TAS100_rr-MEDIAN_20261101-0804_stage6-e-median.xml` names no sr10 run (RunList TAS100a), where P's own XML (written by aurora's path) holds 5 mentions [measured]. The XML's orientations and dipoles are right (Hy 102.814, Ey x2 0 y2 46.5, from the TF's runs) [measured].
- **Where:** `_parse_comments`: `obj, attr_key = key.split(".", 1)`, then `getattr(self, obj).update_attribute(attr_key, value)` inside a bare `except` that logs the warning; the piece is neither set nor appended to `other`, so it is not written to the XML's comments either.
- **Effect:** every EMTF XML written from a TF read from an EDI (scripts/merge_best.py's merged products and Run 3's builders by the same path, this stage's median products) drops the run ids, time periods, sample rates and channel fields that the EDI's INFO block kept, and floods the log (a real warning in such a run is hard to see). Z, errors, frame, channel orientations and geometry are unaffected.
- **Workaround:** none needed for the stage-6 products (the EDI keeps the INFO block, the sidecar names the members); the logs are read with the warnings filtered.
- **Ask:** keep an unmappable `key: value` piece in `other` (the XML's comments) instead of dropping it, and log one summary line per write rather than one per piece.

- **Where:** WAMT_cache_1hz\MBN19.npz (and DATA\MBN19, header 202501250021_mod.INF): MBN19's Hx correlates with MBN18's and MBO21's Hy at +0.91..+1.00 and its Hy with their Hx at +0.91..+1.00 at 20-200 s on 9 of 9 site-days (days 2-6), the direct pairs at -0.25..+0.48; its record means Hx 19, Hy 26,988, Hz -51,013 nT; the control MBN18 "as laid" (+0.98..+0.99). wamt_remotes.rot_h rotates by the mean-field angle (90 deg), which leaves the east component's sign reversed; wamt_align._xcorr_peak returns the largest positive correlation within +-240 s, which for a reversed 20-200 s signal lies near half a period.
- **Effect:** MBN19's clock numbers are contaminated: the fleet's daily lags carry outliers (day 1.5 +26.11 s; after the rebuild days 0.5-2.5 at -1.43, +7.11, +27.61 s), its GNG lags jump between -31 and +31 s (Theil-Sen +1.526 then -0.138 s/day); B3 (g1) and (g3) FAILED at MBN19; its products would carry a mirrored H (an impedance tensor with its H columns exchanged).
- **Workaround:** none in the pre-pass (no untested frame change): MBN19 is out of every pool (GNG-screened; THE SYNC READING's MOVES); the stage stopped at B3.
- **Ask:** the owner and the author: a registered H-swap test at MBN19 (Hx and Hy exchanged at the cache, the H frame reading, the clock re-measured, the fallback "as recorded, flagged"); whether the archive's _mod.INF header records a channel change; GSWA: MBN19.edi's frame. For the estimators: a reversed channel should be refused (a negative peak of |r| >= 0.4), not answered by a side peak.

## 501. MTH5_Aurora_mt-io_2026 processing code (`wamt_run.py` whole-record pass, `camp2026.deliver_full`, `wamt_long.MIN_WINDOWS`) with aurora 0.6.2: a masked product's sixth decimation level is estimated and delivered from as few as 6 windows, and aurora accepts a level from one window, with no count, gate or flag anywhere; wamt_long's MIN_WINDOWS = 15 ("below this the level is not worth shipping") is applied by no campaign path, and the nomask-twin fallback acts only when aurora refuses the level outright (upstream 180) (2026-11-01)
- **Found:** the WA-MT long-period trial (`WAMT_Campaign_2026-10\logs\longperiod_trial_20261101`, TRIAL_GATES.txt 6a3c626b...). Counting the kept runs in aurora's own "Processing Summary Dataframe" of each pass log (floor((n / 4^(L-1) - 256) / 192) + 1 a run), the delivered keys' sixth level (262,144 s windows) holds: MBL22 gng/mask 6 windows (32 kept runs, 4 long enough for one window; both components of Murchison_Oct2024_Run1_EDIs\MBL22.edi), MBM20 hybrid_gng/mask 7 (9 runs), MBU25 partner/mask 10 (28 runs), MBM20 hybrid_gng/nomask 11 (1 run), MBU25 partner/nomask 20 (3 runs) [measured: longperiod_trial_20261101\RUN_WINDOWS.csv; the trial's passes reproduce the delivered rows below 3,000 s at 0 difference, CONTROLS.csv I1]. At MBL22 the delivered rows at 13,211-48,470 s carry phase errors of 12-90 deg and phases outside 0-90 deg in both components where the release's are smooth (65-77 deg) [measured: TRIAL_TABLE.csv]. The delivered products' two record halves agree within their combined bars at 17-47 % of the periods above 3,000 s [measured: VERDICT.csv, J4]. A seventh level built for the trial was estimated by aurora from ONE window (MBU25 partner/mask) and returned with finite VAR, its yx phases 17-99 deg against the sixth level's 60-80 deg [measured: RUN_WINDOWS.csv, TRIAL_TABLE.csv].
- **Where:** `wamt_run.run` / `aurora_pass` compute and log no window count per level; `wamt_long.n_windows` and `MIN_WINDOWS` are used only by wamt_long's own probe; `camp2026.deliver_full` takes the sixth level from the nomask twin only for a product that has no sixth level (upstream 180, `twin_piece`); aurora 0.6.2 (`transfer_function_kernel.valid_decimations`) keeps a level that one run fills with one window.
- **Effect:** the long end of every masked product rests on however many windows the masks leave (the masks cut the record into 9-32 runs where the nomask key has 1-3), and nothing in the EDI, its flags or PRODUCTS.csv says how many; a sixth level from 6 windows is delivered with the same words as one from 20.
- **Workaround:** none (a trial: nothing delivered was changed).
- **Ask (the author's WA chain; the owner):** compute the windows per level from the kept runs (aurora's processing summary, or `wamt_long.n_windows` on `build_keep`'s runs) and write them into the pass's INFO and the delivery's sidecar; under MIN_WINDOWS either flag the level's rows (for example `few_windows`) or take the sixth level from the nomask twin, as the chain already does for a refused level.

## 502. MTH5_Aurora_mt-io_2026 processing code (`wamt_run.aurora_pass`: `logger.remove()` before each aurora call): a pass log holds aurora's "Processing Summary Dataframe" (the kept runs, from which a level's window count follows) for the FIRST remote kind of the process only; every later kind's runs are in no log, so the window counts the owner's ruling of 1 Nov orders into the products table (the few_windows flag, rulings_longperiod_trial 2(a)) cannot be read from the pass logs for most products (2026-11-01)
- **Found:** trial 2 of the long-period trial (`WAMT_Campaign_2026-10\logs\longperiod_trial_20261101\trial2`, TRIAL2_GATES.txt 380ad445...), reading the window counts of the 94 masked whole-record products of record and their nomask twins in the nine deliveries of record of batches 1-4: each production pass log (one process per site and policy, five kinds) holds exactly one processing summary, the first kind's (single); a later kind's count can be inferred only where its header line ("mask drops x% (a+b intervals), N runs, aurora floor ...") equals the first kind's and its remote coverage is 1.0. Counts were found for 52 of 94 products and 41 of 94 twins, for both at 39; the gng kind (61 of the 94) differs from single by the observatory's small gaps (e.g. MBL22 mask: single 31 runs and floor 1.86 %, gng 32 runs and 2.07 %), the partner kind by its coverage [measured: trial2\TRIAL2_WINDOWS.csv]. The inference was checked where a single-kind run exists (trial 1's runs): MBM20 hybrid_gng mask 39 / 7 and nomask 46 / 11 level-5 / level-6 windows, equal both ways (W1).
- **Where:** `wamt_run.aurora_pass` calls `logger.remove()` ("aurora re-arms loguru on import; 40k INFO lines") before `mundi_process.run_aurora`; aurora re-arms its loguru handler only at its first import in the process, so the first kind logs at INFO and every later kind logs nothing; `wamt_run.run` writes no run lengths of its own (runs_wamt.csv has n_runs and the dropped fractions only).
- **Effect:** the kept-run structure (and the level-5/6 window counts) of four kinds in five is lost at every pass of the campaign; a few_windows flag computed "from the pass log" is available for the first kind only, or by a header inference that fails for the observatory and remote-site kinds.
- **Workaround:** none in the trial: counts not logged are reported "n/a (not logged)".
- **Ask (the author's WA chain; the finish of batch 5 on):** write each kind's kept runs (offsets and lengths, or the per-level window counts by `wamt_long.n_windows`) into runs_wamt.csv and the pass's INFO from `build_keep`'s runs, independent of aurora's logger; or keep aurora's processing-summary line at INFO for every call while removing the rest.

WA-MT long-period trial code (`WAMT_Campaign_2026-10\logs\longperiod_trial_20261101\scripts\run_windows.py`, trial 2's count reader of the same form, and the formula quoted in upstream 501 and 502): the window count per decimation level advances the 256-sample window by 192 samples, which is kaiser20_75's OVERLAP, where aurora advances by 64 (windowing_scheme.num_samples_advance = window - overlap; wamt_long.n_windows uses 64), so every window count in the trial's record is 2 to 3 times too low; aurora's own count (num_stft_windows per run and level) stood in the same logs' "Processing Summary Dataframe" and was read by neither trial (2026-11-01)

Trial 2's firing set (the product under 15 at level 6 with the twin above it) is 5 of 39, not 22 (MBL8 xy 1 window, MBI22 yx 1, MBR25 xy 12, WBZ16 yx 12, MBN24 yx 14), under the trial's own threshold of 10 for a verdict, so its registered reading is INCONCLUSIVE, not REFUTED; the decision of the owner's addendum 1 (no policy seam on window count) stands on the count-free readings (the twin's bars no smaller at 38 of 39 components where it holds more windows). ## 513. The author's WA chain (`qld_transients` H tail scan, `wamt_run.scan_e_tails` E tail scan): a one-sample 29,475 nT Hz excursion at MBN07R escapes both transient scans, because the H scan reads only Hx and Hy and the E scan reads only the lines Ex and Ey; the excursion sits two seconds into a new LEMI day file, with a simultaneous one-sample E3 excursion (2026-11-01)
- **Found:** the murchison2_add continuation, 1 Nov 15:36-15:59 WAST, from the figures' reading (MBN07R 01_record.png: "an Hz spike to -80,590 nT"). Files: Murchison_Jan2025\spike_mbn07r.log, regimes_v3_check.log; gates\rulings_batch5_addendum3.md item 1.
- **The sample:** MBN07R sample 4,993,082, 2025-04-21T00:00:02 UTC, day 57.790301. Hz reads -80,589.7 nT against -51,114.6 nT on both sides, an excursion of 29,475 nT. The same second, E3 reads +3,753.5 mV against about -1,780 mV on both sides; E2 and E4 do not jump. Hx and Hy read 25,331.8 and 39.9 nT unchanged from 23:59:59 to 00:00:05. The second is two seconds into a new LEMI day file: a day-boundary artefact of the logger.
- **Where:** `qld_transients.site_events` flags a 600 s chunk on its median 0.1-1 Hz band power of Hx and Hy only (`load_series` reads Hx, Hy). `wamt_run.scan_e_tails` scans the lines Ex and Ey only. MBN07R's Ey line is DEAD in the cache (NaN), so its arms E3 and E4 are unscanned, and the pass's `fill_dead_lines` takes the plain mean of E3+E4. Neither scan reads Hz.
- **Effect:**
  - `build_keep` kept the second under both policies: 6 own-event intervals and 216 E-burst intervals, none over it.
  - The tipper's output channel and the filled y line would have carried the impulse into every window at that second.
- **Workaround:** the regime drop [57.790290, 57.790324] d (the second and one either side), regimes\murchison2_add.json version 3 (761478e3), so the three samples leave under both policies. The registration camp2026_site_events_added.json (6229c1fe) records the finding.
- **Ask:**
  - The author: an Hz term in the H tail scan (or a one-sample excursion test on every channel); the arms of a DEAD line in the E scan where the pass fills that line from them.
  - The skeptic, and the crew if needed: a look at the first seconds of every LEMI day file for such artefacts.

## 517. The author's WA chain (`wamt_run.local` under WAMT_H_LENDER) with camp2026's lent pseudo-site (`camp2026.lenth` lender, the LND_<site>__<lender> keys): a target's own regime drops (set-up, end and record-defect drops) never reach a lent pass, because the drops act only through rot_h(site)'s Hx, Hy and the lent route replaces those channels by the lender's (2026-11-01)
- **Found:** the batch-5 pre-pass skeptic, 1 Nov 2026 16:38-16:40 WAST, checking the LND caches' E and Hz (logs\skeptic_batch5\sk5_b_lnd.csv, sk5_c_lnd.csv; HANDBACK.md (b) and finding M1).
- **Where:** `wamt_run.local` (lines 365-382): `t0r, h, segs = R.rot_h(site)` applies the site's ROT_DROP days to Hx, Hy only; with WAMT_H_LENDER set, Hx and Hy are replaced by `R.rot_h(<LND key>)`, whose NaN pattern is the lender's (camp2026.lenth: `_donor_on_grid(lender, ...)` with the lender's regimes), while Hz and E come from the site's cache unmasked. The drop then removes nothing: the five-channel keep sees finite Hx, Hy, Hz, Ex, Ey on the target's drop days.
- **Effect (murchison2_add, PASS_LIST v2):** LND_MBL10__MBL09's H is finite on all 3,800 samples of MBL10's start drop, where MBL10's Ex (E1+E2) swings -23,719..+11,132 mV/km against a day median of +452; LND_MBL10__MBO07's on all 3,500 samples of MBL10's end drop; LND_MBM10__MBL07's on all 300 samples of MBM10's start drop, where MBM10's Hz departs up to 656 nT from its hours-2-4 median. Every nomask lent product carries those samples; a mask product carries them unless a tail event covers them (the H scan reads the lent Hx, Hy, not the site's).
- **Workaround:** the target's drop days set NaN in the LND pseudo-site's Hx, Hy (a registered change of `camp2026.lenth` lender and a rebuild of the LND keys), or a keep mask for the lent keys that applies under both policies; earlier lent products (batch 1 round 2, batch 4's MBN9) to be checked for target drops.
- **Ask:** The author: `wamt_run.local` could intersect the lender's Hx, Hy with the site's own rot_h finite mask (the site's ROT_DROP days) when WAMT_H_LENDER is set; the owner: a ruling before the batch-5 lent passes.

## 523. The author's processing code (scripts\processing\wamt_copy_test.py; its campaign copy WAMT_Campaign_2026-10\code\copy_test_timedomain.py): a day with no sample enters the copy test, because hp() turns NaN into 0 before the day's finiteness check, and the high-pass ringing of the zero fill is regressed as if it were data
- **Found:** by the F7 skeptic of the murchison2_add finish, 1 Nov 2026 22:20-22:26 WAST (logs\skeptic_batch5_finish\sk5f_series.log, sk5f_probe.log), recomputing the record's MBN19 copy test on the raw day files.
- **Where:** hp(x): `x = np.nan_to_num(np.asarray(x, float) - np.nanmean(x))` before the FFT high-pass at 3,000 s; the day loop then tests `np.isfinite(yy).all()` on the high-passed series, which is always true, and skips only a zero-variance day. A day the cache holds no sample of is zero before the filter and small but non-zero after it.
- **Effect (murchison2_add):** MBN19's cache spans 38.12 days with data on about 21 (raw 2025-01-25 00:22 to 02-14 16:56, 2.3 h on 02-15, 102 s on 03-04; finite 0.545). COPY_TEST_timedomain.csv reads "36 of 38 days" with days 22-37 among the copy days and factors +1.034 / +0.432; on the 22 data days the raw files give 20 of 22 and -15.275 / -0.058. The verdict (GEOLOGY both ways) is unchanged here; a record with empty days elsewhere could be called a copy on ringing alone.
- **Workaround:** none in the record. The skeptic's own test (sk5f_series.copytests) skips a day whose raw line has no finite sample and fills only gaps of 600 s or less before the high-pass.
- **Ask:** test the day's finiteness on the line before hp() (or carry a mask through it) and report the number of days with data beside the days counted; rerun the copy test at any site whose cache has empty days (MBN19 here).

## 525. mt-io (`mt_io.uoa.pr624.read_edl_miniseed`, 0.0.5 as installed in bbmt-2026 from mt-io): a channel file holding two trace ids returns one trace, silently (2026-11-02)

- **What:** the function reads the file with obspy, calls `stream.merge(method=0)` and returns `stream[0]`. A PR6-24 first-hour file written while the logger's station and location codes changed holds two traces with different ids (e.g. `.vic01.Ol.bx` 05:00:00, 1,800 samples; `.vic07.Le.bx` 05:03:00, 34,200), which `merge` does not join; obspy orders the stream by id, so the one kept is whichever sorts first, not the whole hour. `count_samples` on the same file returns the sum, 36,000, so a caller that plans by it and reads by this function gets fewer samples than planned with no error.
- **Where / found:** AusLAMP Victoria (GA eCat 150806) standard copy, 11 of 81 site folders, always the deployment's first hour: VIC011, VIC052, VIC054, VIC059, VIC060, VIC061, VIC063, VIC074, VIC076, VIC078b, VIC087 (`D:\MT_DATA\MT_Victoria_AusLAMP_2013_2018_Workspace\qc\stage1\E1_multitrace_files.csv`). Effect in mt-workbench: workbench issue 76 (seven archives written 28-57 min early).
- **Reproduction:** `python -c "from obspy import read; st=read('E:/MT_Timeseries_DATA/MT_Victoria_AusLAMP_2013_2018/VIC078b/234/VIC078b_140822050000.BX'); print([(t.id,str(t.stats.starttime),t.stats.npts) for t in st]); st.merge(method=0); print(len(st), st[0].stats.npts)"` -> two traces, then `2 1800`; `count_samples` of the file -> 36000.
- **Ask:** read every trace of the file in time order, joining traces that abut at the sample rate whatever their ids (the id change is a logger configuration event, not a new channel), and refuse a file whose traces overlap or leave a gap, naming the file and the traces; `count_samples` and the read must agree by construction.
- **Fixed in the fork 2 Nov 2026** (agent G; patch `surveys/victoria_auslamp_2013_2018/notes/stage1/fix76_mtio.patch`, applied to a worktree of `mt-io` on `mtproc-fixes` at cdceeb3 and installed into bbmt-2026 with `pip install --no-deps`, the ruling R7; uncommitted, commit pending): `_deployment_trace(stream, fn)` returns the LAST trace by start time as the deployment's record and warns once per file naming every trace; overlapping traces raise `TraceOverlapError(ValueError)`; `read_edl_miniseed` and `count_samples` both go through it; new `count_samples_and_start`; `UoAReader` dates a run from the returned trace's start; `UoADataReader.read` re-raises the overlap instead of skipping the file. `tests/uoa/test_pr624_two_trace.py` (12 cases; on the pristine fork 10 fail: 1,800 read, 36,000 counted, no warning, no refusal). tests/uoa 96 passed, 1 skipped.
- **Two findings for the wording of this issue and of the fix** (agent G): (1) in all 55 two-trace channel files of the 11 Victoria stamps the two traces abut with a 0.000 s gap and the data are continuous across the id change (the step at the junction at most 6.3 times the typical sample-to-sample change), which reads as a logger re-coded while running rather than stopped and restarted; the rule "last trace is the record" stands (it drops 2 to 32 min per site, 158 min in all) and a join would also be defensible; (2) `UoACollection.to_dataframe` still dates a file from its NAME, so with this fix alone it reports the two-trace file as 05:00 to 05:57 and splits a run there; the five-line change (date from `count_samples_and_start`) is in agent G's report and is NOT applied (one concern per commit); mt-workbench does not go through `to_dataframe`. Also: mt-io's `find_discontinuities` checks ASCII files only; miniSEED contiguity is unchecked in the library and is now guarded in mt-workbench (workbench 76).

## 526. aurora (fork 0.6.2+mtproc at aurora, `RME_RR.compute_inverse_signal_covariance` and the merged `cov_ss_inv` exported as the TF's inverse_signal_power): the remote-reference inverse signal power, and so every Z error, changes when one local input channel is negated, while Z itself is reproduced exactly (2026-11-04)

- **Found:** by agent D2 of the Tasmania broadband 2016 track, 4 Nov 2026 09:0x WAST, in the oracle of the declared flips (surveys/tasmania_broadband_2016/notes/stage2/README_flips.md, "Re-ingest and declared-frame products"). Tas-W330 was re-ingested with its hy coil declared reversed (`flip_h: [hy]`: the stored hy samples negated, chain unchanged) and its two lines declared reversed (dipole gains +L instead of -L), and reprocessed rr Tas-W344 with every setting of its v1 product (`--tag v1o --no-masks`; v1 had no mask).
- **Where:** `<ws>/tf/Tas-W330_rr-Tas-W344_20261103-1909_v1.*` against `..._20261104-0848_v1o.*` (D:/MT_DATA/MT_Tasmania_Broadband_2016_Workspace). Same code (mt_workbench 929317c uncommitted, aurora record_sha256 f9c87c8b0893), same remote archive, same band scheme and tweaks.
- **Effect:** Z of v1o equals v1 with rows x, y and column y negated EXACTLY (all 58 periods, every element, max relative difference 0.0), but every Z error differs, by up to 0.62 relative (e.g. 0.0056 s: Zxy error 0.165 in v1, 0.062 in v1o). In the XML products the residual covariance diagonal is unchanged (ratio 1.000) and the inverse signal power diagonal is not (ratio 0.30 for hx, 0.14 for hy at the first period). A sign change of one input is D = diag(1, -1); a correct inverse signal covariance transforms as D S D, whose diagonal, and so every error, is invariant. Line-only flips (outputs) leave the errors exact (Tas-W302: Z and errors identical to 0.0), so only an INPUT sign reaches the error.
- **Workaround:** none applied. The declared-frame products of the Tasmania track (v1d, v2d) carry the errors of the products they negate; at Tas-W330 these are not what a rerun from the declared archive gives. Which of the two error sets is right is not established.
- **Ask:** find the term of the RR error path that is not equivariant under a sign change of an input channel (candidates: the robust-weighted X and Z used in compute_inverse_signal_covariance, the merging of cov_ss_inv over decimation levels, or a real/abs taken of a complex off-diagonal before the diagonal is read); a unit test: negate hy in a synthetic RR problem and require Z negated in column y and all errors unchanged.

## 527. MTH5_Aurora_mt-io_2026 processing code (`camp2026.etails._check_arithmetic`, called by etails.build before a variant's E-burst scan is registered): a production scan that holds zero power in a chunk (a railed line's constant stretch) makes the relative difference 0 / 0 = nan, and "not rel < 1e-9" refuses the build although the arithmetic reproduces the stored scan exactly
- **Found:** by the murchison2_add finish part 2a agent, 1 Nov 2026 23:04-23:07 WAST (Murchison_Jan2025\finish\etails_variants.log), building the mask-policy E-burst scans of the E-line variant caches (code\scratchpad\finish\etails_variants_jan25.sh). - **Where:** `rel = float(np.max(np.abs(a[ok] - b[ok]) / np.abs(b[ok])))` over the chunks finite in both scans; a 600 s chunk of a constant series has Welch power exactly 0 in the stored scan and in the recomputed one, so that chunk divides 0 by 0.
- **Effect (murchison2_add):** MBN07R's production Ex is E1 alone, railed at -47,795.195 mV/km from day 38 (31 of 69 days); every build of MBN07R's variant scans (r6armA, r6armB, r6mean) raised "tails_murchison2_add_e\MBN07R.npz Ex: relative difference nan against the stored scan", so no variant of MBN07R can run under the mask policy by the registered route; the 42 other registrations (14 targets) read Ex 0.0 / Ey 0.0, and the resumed part 2a's two more (r6armA MBN07, r6mean MBN11r, 4 Nov 09:28) also. MBN07R's y-line variants were run hybrid_gng/nomask (its product of record's kind under the other policy), recorded in the arm choice.
- **Workaround:** none in the record (the variants of the one site run under nomask).
- **Ask:** take the difference where |b| > 0 and require a == b exactly where b == 0 (or compare max |a - b| against max |b|), so a reproduced zero-power chunk passes and a non-zero one where the stored scan holds zero still fails.

## 536. MTH5_Aurora_mt-io_2026 processing code (`camp2026.bandrule.plant_half`, the remove_ramp form): the 0.50 control's copy carries 6-10 % more Welch power than Hx at 20-200 s on days with a strong daily variation (2026-11-04)
- **Found:** by the batch 6 (esperance2026) pre-pass, gate B5 (e) [Esperance_Mar2024\BANDRULE_control.csv]: at MBW20 the plant's corrected coherence is 0.4999 / 0.5165 / 0.5319 (the target 0.50 +- 0.05 met in every band) but the copy/Hx Welch power is 1.0973 at 20-200 s (1.0219 and 1.0154 at 200-2,000 and 2,000-10,000 s) against the registered 1.00 +- 0.05; POST HOC at MBV23 1.0596 at 20-200 s. Batch 5's MBN14 gave 0.998 (Murchison days). The control FAILED as registered and stays failed (rulings_batch6 item 6); the band rule's calls stand (the quantity it reads, the corrected coherence, behaved; the DEAD lines sit an order of magnitude under 0.50).
- **Cause (read, not fixed):** the copy is the phase-randomised DFT of the de-meaned, ramp-free day; the remove_ramp form (upstream 352) takes out the end-to-end jump but not the derivative discontinuity of the day's periodic extension, which leaks broadband power that is a larger fraction of Hx's own power at 20-200 s where Esperance's Hx spectrum is red and quiet.
- **Ask:** a day taper (Hann or Tukey over the day's edges, with the taper's power loss compensated) or a two-day DFT with the copy cut from the middle day, so the copy's band power equals Hx's within 2 % in every band; a unit test on a synthetic day with a diurnal sine plus red noise. Until then the next gate registers the 20-200 s power as a reading and keeps the criterion at the two longer bands (lesson 49).

- **Found:** by the batch 6 (esperance2026) pre-pass Part 1b [Esperance_Mar2024\RUN_LOG.md 16:06:49; store_rebuild.log]: rulings_batch6 item 11 ordered the store rebuilt in place for four targets (MBV24, MBW26, MBW25, MBY21) after the regimes table changed. build_store(batch, targets=[...]) rewrites camp2026_store_table.csv for the whole batch (76 -> 79 rows only because the agent merged the write inside the process), and with force=True it would also recut the GNG window and recompute the fleet weights, which were not ruled to change; restore_targets (the campaign's own re-store helper) refuses MBW25 and MBW26 because they are pool sites. The agent moved the 30 production files aside (kept under logs\esperance2026\store_before_rebuild_esp26\) and bound the table merge in its process: a process binding, not a code change.
- **Ask:** build_store(targets=...) updates only the named targets' rows of the store table (the other rows byte for byte), never touches the GNG window, its mask or the fleet weights unless a separate flag says so, and restore_targets accepts a pool site when the caller says the fleet weights are to stay as built (a `keep_weights=True` argument), recording in camp2026_store_notes.txt which regimes table each target was built under (the two-table rule of B7 (e) then reads the note instead of file times).

## 538. mt_metadata (the EDI reader, `mt_metadata.transfer_functions.io.edi`, as installed in bbmt-2026): a free-text INFO processing-parameter value holding "(10-3,000 s median," is parsed as a date and the read of the EDI fails (2026-11-04)
- **Found:** by agent G in the Tasmania broadband Run 1 build, flags pass 2 at Tas-W300 [`surveys/tasmania_broadband_2016/notes/stage4/README_run1.md`, "The tail redone after the issue 91 fix"; the refused EDI kept in `<ws>\qc\stage4\superseded_flags_pass2_failed_20261104\`]: a site-fact flag written as an INFO line `transfer_function.processing_parameters.mt_workbench.flag_...=yx 0.185 dex below the long-period twin TAS300 (10-3,000 s median, at equal phase)` made the reader raise on the read-back; the same line without parentheses and commas reads cleanly.
- **Where:** the INFO block parser hands every `key=value` pair to the metadata setters, and a value that looks date-like to the date parser (digits, a hyphen, a comma) is tried as a date instead of being kept as text; the free-text processing-parameter values that the mt-workbench flags and the as-laid lines write (the mechanism of merge_best and the Run finalizers) are not declared as text anywhere the reader could know.
- **Effect:** a delivered EDI whose flag text holds a period range with a comma cannot be read back by mt_metadata (and so not by the workbench's checks), although other readers take the line as text; the fact text had to be reworded.
- **Workaround:** flag and fact texts in INFO lines carry no parentheses or commas around digit groups (the Run 1 wording "over 10 to 3000 s"); the test that failed is the read-back of every delivered EDI, kept.
- **Ask:** the INFO parser keeps a processing-parameter value as text unless its key names a date field, and never raises on a value it cannot parse.

## 548. mt-io 0.0.5 (`lemi.lemi424.LEMI424.run_metadata` / `to_run_ts`): every channel of a LEMI-424 run has `measurement_azimuth` 0.0 (by and e2 included) and e1, e2 `dipole_length` 0.0 (2026-11-05)
- **Found:** by the Victoria AusLAMP stage 6.0 smoke (agent S) [`D:\MT_DATA\MT_Victoria_AusLAMP_LEMI424_2016_2018_Workspace\qc\stage6\smoke\G2_archives.csv`]: the archives of VIC004R, VIC009R and VIC058R read back with h5py hold by and e2 at azimuth 0.0 and e1, e2 at dipole_length 0.0. GA's release MTH5 of the same records holds 0/90 and 88/100 m.
- **Where:** `run_metadata` adds `Electric(component=e1|e2)` and `Magnetic(component=bx|by|bz)` with default metadata; `to_run_ts` sets the units only.
- **Effect:** anything that reads channel azimuths (an EDI writer's EMEAS/HMEAS, a rotation) takes by and e2 as north. The samples are unaffected.
- **Workaround:** mt-workbench to set them from survey.yaml (workbench 94); the smoke's W1 wrapper does it.
- **Ask:** the reader sets by and e2 to 90 deg and takes the dipole lengths from the `.INF` `%L1 %L2` when one is beside the file.
- **Worked around in mt-workbench, 5 Nov 2026 (agent T, workbench 94, uncommitted):** `instruments.lemi424_stored` sets the azimuths (hx 0, hy 90, hz 0 with tilt 90, ex 0, ey 90) and the ex/ey dipole lengths from survey.yaml when it renames the channels; the reader itself is unchanged, so the ask stands.

## 549. mt-io 0.0.5 (`lemi.lemi424.lemi_parse_position_columns` / `lemi_position_parser`): one line whose GPS block lost a field stops the read of the whole file with "ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'S'" (or 'E') (2026-11-05)
- **Found:** by the Victoria AusLAMP stage 6.1 ingest (agent U) [`D:\MT_DATA\MT_Victoria_AusLAMP_LEMI424_2016_2018_Workspace\logs\ingest_VIC051R.log`, `_VIC033R`, `_VIC069R`]: VIC051R `DATA0039/201712240000.TXT` line 41267 reads "2017 12 24 11 27 46 21557.398 7.077 -55249.156 23.59 28.88 163.363 -298.924 14.471 -9.973 13.00 138.2 S 4 E 2 0 17 6" (24 fields; the latitude is missing, so 'S' lands in the latitude column); VIC033R `DATA0060/201801090000.TXT` line 78165 has 22 fields ("324.1  S  E 0 0 0"). Six such lines at three of 19 cards (VIC033R 3, VIC069R 2, VIC051R 1), counted from the raw files with awk on fields 18-21.
- **Where:** `lemi_parse_position_columns` maps every distinct value of the latitude/longitude columns through `lemi_position_parser`, which calls `float(position)` (line 107) with no guard; called from `LEMI424.read` (lines 647, 676, 712, 773).
- **Effect:** the file, and with it the whole site in mt-workbench (workbench 99), cannot be read, although every data column of the damaged line is sound.
- **Workaround:** none taken in this stage (the sites were left out as the brief orders); a cleaned copy of the six lines, or a wrapper in the agent's process, would read them.
- **Ask:** parse the position columns with `pd.to_numeric(errors="coerce")` (NaN for a damaged value) and the hemisphere columns only where they are N/S/E/W, so a GPS dropout costs the line's position, not the file; count such lines in the read's log.

## 550. mth5 0.6.9 (`mth5/__init__.py`, `CHANNEL_SUMMARY_DTYPE` and `RUN_SUMMARY_DTYPE`: `("survey", "S30")`): a survey id longer than 30 characters is cut in the channel and run summaries, and every aurora run then fails with "Could not find /Experiment/Surveys/<first 30 characters>/..." (2026-11-05)
- **Found:** by the Eastern Goldfields long-period pilot (stage 3, agent H; verified by the owner in the installed package) [`surveys/eastern_goldfields_lp_2018_2019/notes/stage3/HANDBACK_agentH.md`, defect H3; `tables/ledger.csv`]: the survey id `eastern_goldfields_lp_2018_2019` has 31 characters; every `process_rr.py` run stops in 10 to 40 s with "Could not find /Experiment/Surveys/eastern_goldfields_lp_2018_201/Stations/EGFLP22/sr10_0003". The ingest, the decimation, the Gingin archive and the stack builder all worked on the same archives, so nothing warned before the first processing run, two full ingests later.
- **Where:** `mth5/__init__.py` lines 89 and 114 (`("survey", "S30")`); the TF summary's field is S50 (line 70) and `groups/survey.py` line 99 uses U10. The run summary built from the channel summary (`RunSummary.from_mth5s`) hands the cut id to aurora's `KernelDataset`, which builds the group path from it.
- **Effect:** a survey whose id is longer than 30 characters ingests and reads, and cannot be processed. The cut is silent: no error at ingest, none when the summary is written.
- **Workaround:** none in place on 5 Nov 2026 (the owner's question to the author: a workbench-side repair of the id in `mt_workbench.process.kernel_dataset`, a shorter survey id with a re-ingest, or the wider field).
- **Ask:** one width for the survey id in every summary table, wide enough for real ids (64 or more), and an error at write time when an id would be cut, in place of the silent cut.
- **Worked around in mt-workbench, 5 Nov 2026 (agent I, workbench 108, by decision, uncommitted):** `process._restore_survey_ids`, called in `kernel_dataset` after `from_mth5s`, puts each archive's own survey id back into the run summary's rows (field width read from mth5; archives opened read-only; a ValueError on an ambiguous prefix); `tests/survey_id_cut_unit.py` (7 cases). Proof: EGFLP22 rr EGFLP30, whole record, wrote its EDI in 692 s. Not repaired, and not reached by `process_rr.py`: the summary tables stored inside the archives, the Fourier-coefficient summary (also 30 characters), station ids longer than 30.

## 551. mt-io 0.0.5 (`phoenix.readers.mtu.mtu_table.MTUTable._read_latitude` / `_read_longitude`): an MTU-5A table's degree-minute position "DDMM.mmm,H" is read as DDMM.mmm / 100, not DD + MM.mmm/60, so every station is misplaced, by up to 4.9 km north-south and 8.9 km east-west at Oak Dam (2026-11-06)
- **Found:** by the Oak Dam scout, reader I (inventory) [`2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\oak_dam\results\scout_20261106\report_inventory.md`, "Defect candidates" (a) 1]; reproduced by the filing agent on 6 Nov 2026 at 13:45 on a December 2019 table.
- **Reproduction:** mt-io 0.0.5 as installed in bbmt-2026 (from `mt-io.worktrees/mtproc-fixes`), Python 3.11.16. File `D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191207\4573C06A.TBL` (LATG "3103.188,S", LNGG "13700.782,E"). `from mt_io.phoenix.readers import MTUTable; t = MTUTable(r"<file>"); print(t.station_metadata.location.latitude, t.station_metadata.location.longitude)`. Expected -31.053133, 137.013033. Observed -31.03188, 137.00782 (2.36 km north and 0.50 km west of the table's position).
- **Where:** `mt_io/phoenix/readers/mtu/mtu_table.py` lines 430 and 466 (`value = float(parts[0]) / 100.0`). Both docstrings give the right answer (41.006467 for "4100.388,N"); the code does not.
- **Effect:** every MTU-5A position mt-io returns is wrong. Over the 247 Oak Dam tables the error reaches 4.9 km north-south and 8.9 km east-west [inventory, measured]. For an MTU-5A ingest: site positions, inter-site distances and remote pairing cannot be taken from `MTUTable.station_metadata`.
- **Workaround:** the mt-workbench `mtu5a` reader (`src/mt_workbench/mtu5a.py`, workbench 117) decodes the position itself as degrees plus minutes / 60 (`table_degrees`) and does not use `MTUTable`. The scout's tables convert the raw string themselves.
- **Ask:** `deg = int(x // 100); value = deg + (x - 100 * deg) / 60`, plus a test on the docstring examples.

## 552. mt-io 0.0.5 (`MTUTable.station_metadata`, `run_metadata` and the channel metadata): the time period is taken from STIM/ETIM, the instrument's schedule window, not from FTIM/LTIM, the recording; every Oak Dam station, run and channel is dated 2019-01-01 .. 2022-01-02 (2026-11-06)
- **Found:** by the Oak Dam scout, readers I and R [`2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\oak_dam\results\scout_20261106\`: `report_inventory.md` (a) 2, `report_reader.md` section 6 P7]; reproduced by the filing agent on 6 Nov 2026 at 13:42 and 13:45.
- **Reproduction:** mt-io 0.0.5 (bbmt-2026, as in 551). (1) `t = MTUTable(r"D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191207\4573C06A.TBL"); print(t.station_metadata.time_period.start, t.station_metadata.time_period.end, t.run_metadata.time_period.start, t.ex_metadata.time_period.start)`. Expected the table's FTIM .. LTIM, 2019-12-06T23:04:47 .. 2019-12-07T07:32:55 (the EPR's Interval and the TS4's length agree). Observed 2019-01-01T00:00:00+00:00 .. 2022-01-02T00:00:00+00:00, with the same start for the run and for ex. (2) The scout's `scripts\reader_trial.py defects --folder D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191207 --recording 4759C07A --log <log>`, item D7. Expected 2019-12-07T01:09:50 .. 05:20:26. Observed 2019-01-01 .. 2022-01-02. Every RunTS then warns "end time of dataset ... does not match metadata end 2022-01-02T00:00:00+00:00".
- **Where:** `mtu_table.py` 583-584 (the station) and the channels at 679-683, 724-727, 768-771, 812-815 and 855-858; the class docstring (64-65) calls STIM the "starting time". In all 247 Oak Dam tables STIM is 2019-01-01 00:00:00 and ETIM is 2022-01-02 00:00:00 [inventory, measured].
- **Effect:** for an MTU-5A ingest, no time span from mt-io's table metadata can be used: not for overlap search, not for remote pairing by time, and not as an archive's time period.
- **Workaround:** the mt-workbench `mtu5a` reader (`src/mt_workbench/mtu5a.py`, workbench 117) times each run from the record tags (`walk_tags`) and takes a site's span from the tables' FTIM and LTIM decoded by type byte (`span`); it does not use `MTUTable`.
- **Ask:** take the time period from FTIM .. LTIM, once LTIM is decoded; keep STIM/ETIM as schedule fields.

## 553. mt-io 0.0.5 (`phoenix.readers.mtu.mtu_ts.MTUTSN.to_runts`): the first record tag's time is assigned to `channel_metadata.start_time`, which is not a field, so it is discarded; every RunTS of an MTU-5A file starts at the table's STIM (2019-01-01 at Oak Dam) (2026-11-06)
- **Found:** by the Oak Dam scout, reader R [`2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\oak_dam\results\scout_20261106\report_reader.md`, section 6 P1]; reproduced by the filing agent on 6 Nov 2026 at 13:42.
- **Reproduction:** mt-io 0.0.5 (bbmt-2026, as in 551). The scout's `scripts\reader_trial.py defects --folder D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191207 --recording 4759C07A --log <log>`, item D3: `read_phoenix(r"...\191207\4759C07A.TS4").start`. Expected 2019-12-07T01:09:50+00:00, the first record tag. Observed 2019-01-01T00:00:00+00:00; the RunTS's own end is then 2019-01-01T04:10:36.99.
- **Where:** `mtu_ts.py` line 617 (`channel_metadata.start_time = ts_metadata["start"]`). `start_time` is not among the model fields of mt_metadata's `Electric` (checked), and the assignment raises nothing. The RunTS keeps the `time_period.start` that `MTUTable` set from STIM (552).
- **Distinct from 552:** fixing the table alone would not fix the start. For 4573C06A, FTIM is 2019-12-06 23:04:47 while the TS3's first tag is 23:05:15, 28 s later [measured by the filing agent, 13:43].
- **Effect:** every sample of every MTU-5A RunTS is mis-dated, here by about 11 months. For an MTU-5A ingest, `to_runts` / `read_phoenix` output cannot be archived as it stands; the start must come from the first tag.
- **Workaround:** the mt-workbench `mtu5a` reader (`src/mt_workbench/mtu5a.py`, workbench 117) does not call `to_runts`: each run starts at its first record's tag (`walk_tags`, `read_run`).
- **Ask:** set `channel_metadata.time_period.start` from the first tag. Give the burst bands per-record times (554).

## 554. mt-io 0.0.5 (`MTUTSN.read`): every record of an MTU-5A TS file is stacked end to end under the first record's tag, so a burst band (TS2, TS3) comes back as one contiguous series with its gaps lost (2026-11-06)
- **Found:** by the Oak Dam scout, reader R [`2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\oak_dam\results\scout_20261106\report_reader.md`, section 6 P2 and section 3]; reproduced by the filing agent on 6 Nov 2026 at 13:42.
- **Reproduction:** mt-io 0.0.5 (bbmt-2026, as in 551). The scout's `scripts\reader_trial.py defects --folder D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191207 --recording 4759C07A --log <log>`, item D4: `read_phoenix(r"...\191207\4759C07A.TS3")`. Expected the bursts kept apart: 501 bursts of 2 x 1 s records every 30 s, spanning 15002 s by the tags. Observed one contiguous series of n 2404800, from 2019-01-01T00:00:00 to 00:16:41.9996, with no gap marks. Reader R measured the same on 4573C06A: TS3 presents 2032 s as continuous over a tag span of 30452 s, and TS2 (0.1 s records 1 s apart, 4 per burst, every 30 s) presents 406.4 s over 30453 s.
- **Where:** `mtu_ts.py` 532-565. `n_block = round(file_size / record size)` is followed by every block written into one array, and the tag dict keeps the first record's `start` only.
- **Effect:** any spectrum, filter or decimation across a joined burst edge is corrupt, and the series is mis-timed after the first record. For an MTU-5A ingest, the burst bands cannot go through `MTUTSN.read` / `read_phoenix`; only the continuous TS4 can (workbench 120).
- **Workaround:** the mt-workbench `mtu5a` reader (`src/mt_workbench/mtu5a.py`, workbench 117) walks the tags itself and ends a run where they step by other than 1 s (`plan_runs`); `read_run` refuses a file whose record and scan counts by mt-io differ from the walk's.
- **Ask:** return each record's start time (or one segment per contiguous run of records), as `DecimatedSegmentCollection` does for the 5C `.td_24k`.

## 555. mt-io 0.0.5 (`MTUTable._get_dictionary_from_tbl` and `decode_tbl_value`): table values are decoded by a hard-coded name map that ignores each block's own type byte (byte 11); 67 of the 139 tags of an Oak Dam table are misread, among them SRL2, LTIM, MODE, EXR/EYR and STDE, and every time string is malformed (2026-11-06)
- **Found:** by the Oak Dam scout, readers I and R [`2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\oak_dam\results\scout_20261106\`: `report_inventory.md` (a) 3 and 7, `report_reader.md` section 6 P8]; reproduced by the filing agent on 6 Nov 2026 at 13:43 to 13:45.
- **Reproduction:** mt-io 0.0.5 (bbmt-2026, as in 551). `t = MTUTable(r"D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191207\4573C06A.TBL"); print({k: t.tbl_dict.get(k, "<absent>") for k in ("SRL2", "MODE", "MXSC", "LTIM", "LTIME", "STDE", "EXR", "EYR", "EXPR", "TSYN", "FTIM", "HTIM")})`.
  - Expected (decoded by the block's type byte: 0 int32, 1 float64, 2/4 string, 5 time as sec, min, hour, day, month, yy, weekday, century; the weekday byte matches the calendar on every set time except ETIM, a schedule value): SRL2 24000, MODE 9, MXSC 2400, LTIM 2019-12-07T07:32:55, STDE -1, EXR 77, EYR 51, EXPR 45.0743, TSYN 2019-12-06T23:02:00, FTIM 2019-12-06T23:04:47, HTIM unset (all-zero bytes).
  - Observed: SRL2 'À]', MODE '', MXSC '`', LTIM '7 \x07\x07\x0c\x13\x06\x14', LTIME absent, STDE 2.1219957905e-314, EXR 'M', EYR '3', EXPR 'xÿj\x0c\x83\x89F@', TSYN '\x02\x17\x06\x0c\x13\x05\x14', FTIM '2019-12-06-T23:04:47', HTIM '2000-00-00-T00:00:00'.
  - A comparison of every block against the type-byte decode: 67 of the 139 tags differ, plus the trailing non-tag block (562). The inventory found the same 67 in all 247 Oak Dam tables. The scout's `reader_trial.py defects` (as in 553), items D8 and D9, shows the same on 4759C07A, with `ex_metadata.contact_resistance.start` 0.0 against TBL EXR 'c' (2659).
- **Where:** `mtu_table.py` 143-211 (`TBL_TAG_TYPES`: LTIM spelled "LTIME" at 168; EXR and EYR absent; STDE and STDH typed double, though the file stores int32), 325-328 (an unlisted tag falls back to "char"), and 256 (the time string, with a stray "-" before "T", the century fixed at "20" and byte 7 ignored).
- **Effect:** the TS2 rate, the recording end, the contact and electrode resistances, the GPS sync times and the DSP settings cannot be read through mt-io. For an MTU-5A ingest, the table must be decoded independently of `tbl_dict`.
- **Workaround:** the mt-workbench `mtu5a` reader (`src/mt_workbench/mtu5a.py`, workbench 117) decodes each 25-byte block by its own type byte (`read_table`).
- **Ask:** decode each block by its byte 11 and keep the name map for descriptions only; build ISO times with the century from byte 7, and return None for an all-zero time.

## 556. mt-io 0.0.5 (`MTUTable.station_metadata`): a SITE holding a space or "!" goes straight into `Station.id` and raises a pydantic ValidationError, so the time series of such a recording cannot be read through `read_phoenix` at all (2026-11-06)
- **Found:** by the Oak Dam scout, reader I [`2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\oak_dam\results\scout_20261106\report_inventory.md`, (a) 4]; reproduced by the filing agent on 6 Nov 2026 at 13:44 and 13:45, with the read failure added.
- **Reproduction:** mt-io 0.0.5 (bbmt-2026, as in 551). (1) `t2 = MTUTable(r"D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191212-13\4573C12B.TBL"); t2.station_metadata`, with SITE 'REMOTE b', a December 2019 remote recording. (2) `read_phoenix(r"D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191212-13\4573C12B.TS4")`. Expected a Station with a sanitised id and the name kept, then a RunTS. Observed, both times, "ValidationError: 1 validation error for Station id String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$' [type=string_pattern_mismatch, input_value='REMOTE b', ...]".
- **Where:** `mtu_table.py` 571 (`station.id = self.tbl_dict.get("SITE", ...)`), reached from `MTUTSN.to_runts` (`mtu_ts.py` 604) through `survey_metadata` (`mtu_table.py` 534). mt-io's 5C path already replaces spaces (`receiver_metadata.py` 550); the MTU path does not.

- **Ask:** sanitise the id as the 5C path does, and keep the raw SITE (for example in `geographic_name`).

## 557. mt-io 0.0.5 (`MTUTSN.to_runts(calibrate=True)`): the scale factors are applied to the reader's own `self.ts` in place, and the RunTS shares that memory; a second call scales again, and the first RunTS changes after the fact (2026-11-06)
- **Found:** by the Oak Dam scout, reader R [`2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\oak_dam\results\scout_20261106\report_reader.md`, section 6 P5]; reproduced by the filing agent on 6 Nov 2026 at 13:42.
- **Reproduction:** mt-io 0.0.5 (bbmt-2026, as in 551). The scout's `scripts\reader_trial.py defects --folder D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191207 --recording 4759C07A --log <log>`, item D5: `o = MTUTSN(<4759C07A.TS4>); r1 = o.to_runts(table_filepath=<4759C07A.TBL>, calibrate=True); r2 = o.to_runts(table_filepath=<TBL>, calibrate=True)`. Expected ex[0] = 87268 counts x 0.000730157 = 63.7193 mV/km both times. Observed r1 ex[0] 63.7193 and r2 ex[0] 0.0465251, a ratio of 0.000730157, scaled twice; r1's ex[0] now also reads 0.0465251.
- **Where:** `mtu_ts.py` 638 (`ts[channel_index, :] = ts[channel_index, :] * scale_factor` on `self.ts`) and 643-647 (each ChannelTS wraps a view of that array).
- **Effect:** any caller that builds a RunTS twice from one reader (once to inspect and once to archive, say) gets values scaled by the factor again, silently, and its earlier RunTS is corrupted too. For an MTU-5A ingest, one `to_runts` per fresh reader at most.
- **Workaround:** the mt-workbench `mtu5a` reader (`src/mt_workbench/mtu5a.py`, workbench 117) stores the counts of `MTUTSN.read()` and does not call `to_runts`.
- **Ask:** scale a copy, or keep counts and record the factor as a filter (558).

- **Found:** by the Oak Dam scout, reader R [`2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\oak_dam\results\scout_20261106\report_reader.md`, section 6 P6 and section 4]; reproduced by the filing agent on 6 Nov 2026 at 13:42.

Expected H in nT only once a coil response is applied, or else counts or volts with every applied factor and the response recorded as filters. Observed: ex and ey "milliVolt per kilometer", hx, hy and hz "nanoTesla", `filters []` on all five.

For an MTU-5A ingest, store counts with the scalar chain recorded as filters; the response is a separate decision (workbench 119).
