## 563. aurora 0.6.2+mtproc (`ConfigCreator.create_from_kernel_dataset`): a `remote_channels` argument is accepted and then dropped, so the decimation levels get no reference channels and every level fails in RME_RR with "list index out of range" (2026-11-06)
- **Found:** by agent E of the Victoria short-end pilot (S8, an electric reference), 6 Nov 2026 14:03, on a diagnostic run that passed `remote_channels=["hx", "hy"]` through `mt_workbench.process.process_station(**config_kwargs)` [`<ws>\qc\stage5\short_end_pilot\logs\jobs\S8proof_VIC088.log`; driver `surveys\victoria_auslamp_2013_2018\notes\stage5\se_s8_process_rr.py`].
- **Reproduction:** bbmt-2026. `process_station(lh5, "VIC088", rh5, "VIC092", band_scheme=..., remote_channels=["hx", "hy"])` on the Victoria scratch archives. Expected the same TF as without the argument (hx, hy are the default reference). Observed: at every decimation level `process_transfer_functions_with_weights` and the unweighted fallback fail with `IndexError: list index out of range` in `RME_RR.__init__` (line 28), the levels are skipped, and aurora returns a TransferFunctionCollection, which process_station refuses.
- **Where:** `aurora/config/config_creator.py` 249-251. The block sets `decimation_obj.reference_channels = kernel_dataset.remote_channels` only when `remote_channels is None`; when it is given, nothing is assigned (no else branch), so `reference_channels` stays [] and the remote dataset is empty in the regression.
- **Effect:** a reference other than the remote hx, hy (for example a remote electric reference) cannot be asked for through the config creator. Without the argument nothing changes. No product of record is affected.
- **Workaround:** set `reference_channels` on every decimation of the built config (the diagnostic driver wraps `mt_workbench.process.build_config` for that run; no code under src/ changed).
- **Ask:** add `else: decimation_obj.reference_channels = remote_channels`.

## 564. mt-io 0.0.5 (`MTUTSN.read`, `MTUTSN._read_header`): the record tags' status (byte 14) and saturation flags (byte 15) are stepped over and never exposed, so the receiver's own per-record clip marks are lost; on an Oak Dam remote recording, 4933 flagged records (739,804 ex samples at the clip) come back with no flag anywhere (2026-11-06)
- **Found:** by the Oak Dam scout, reader H [`2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\oak_dam\results\scout_20261106\logs\reader_h_reply.txt`, "Package defect candidate"; `logs\reader_h.log` 13:58:06 and 13:58:41]; reproduced by the notes pass on 6 Nov 2026 at 14:04:43 to 14:04:47, with the criterion stated before the run (not reproduced if the raw tags held no 4933 flagged records, or if any attribute of the reader or key of `ts_metadata` carried status or saturation).
- **Reproduction:** mt-io 0.0.5 (bbmt-2026, as in 551). File `D:\MT_DATA\MT_Oak_Dam\01-RAW\01-RAW\191207-08\4573C07A.TS4` (the December 2019 remote, 184,287,474 bytes, 80,757 records of 1 s at 150 Hz). (1) Own walk of the tags (record = 32-byte tag + 150 scans x 5 channels x 3 bytes; the walk ends exactly at end of file): byte 15 is 0x01 on 4933 records and 0 on 75,824; byte 14 is 0x03 on exactly those 4933 records and 0 elsewhere. (2) `from mt_io.phoenix.readers import MTUTSN; o = MTUTSN(r"<file>"); o.read(); print(list(vars(o)), list(o.ts_metadata))`. Expected the per-record status and saturation (as arrays, a mask or at least a count) somewhere on the reader. Observed: attributes `_p16`, `_p8`, `_accepted_extensions`, `_file_path`, `ts`, `ts_metadata`; `ts_metadata` keys `box_number`, `ts_type`, `sample_rate`, `n_ch`, `n_scan`, `start`, `ts_length`, `n_block`; no status or saturation anywhere (`__getstate__`, inherited from `object`, returns the same six attributes). The samples themselves are read: ex of `o.ts` holds 739,804 values with |count| >= 0.94 x 2^23 (largest 7,895,314).
- **Where:** `mt_io/phoenix/readers/mtu/mtu_ts.py` 282 (`_read_header`: `ts_fid.seek(4, 1)` steps over bytes 14-17 of the first tag), 391 (`_process_data_block`: `ts_fid.seek(32, 1)` steps over every record's tag) and 556-568 (the `ts_metadata` dict). The module's own docstring (lines 26-27) documents byte 14 as the status code and byte 15 as the bit-wise saturation flags. By the same reading of the code, the clock status (byte 21) is skipped too (line 287).
- **Effect:** the MTU-5A clips at about 0.941 of full scale (+-7,893,675 to 7,893,687 counts, dithering over three codes) [reader H, measured], so a caller cannot find the saturation from the samples with a full-scale rail test either; the tag byte is the receiver's own record of it. It agrees with the samples (every Oak Dam TS4 record holding samples at the clip carries the bit of that channel, bit = channel number - 1) and with the contractor's "Saturated" counts (the scout's check RH1, 14 of 14 recordings). Through mt-io, a clipped channel reaches an archive unmarked. For an MTU-5A ingest: walk the tags independently (the scout's `scripts\mtu_decode.py`, `walk_tags`) or extend the reader.
- **Workaround:** the mt-workbench `mtu5a` reader (`src/mt_workbench/mtu5a.py`, workbench 117) reads the status and saturation bytes from its own walk of the tags and writes them to the archive's `mtu5a_flags.csv` (`write_flags`); they are not applied as masks (workbench 123).
- **Ask:** keep bytes 14, 15 and 21 of every record's tag (per-record arrays on the reader, say `status`, `saturation`, `clock_status`), and carry the saturation bits per channel into the RunTS as a mask or a per-channel count.

## 565. mt-io 0.0.5 (`MTUTSN.read`, `MTUTSN._read_header`): the record tags' clock status (byte 21) and clock error (bytes 22-25) are stepped over and never exposed, as bytes 14-15 are (564), so the receiver's per-record clock quality is lost; on a Roxby recording, 176 records with a non-zero clock error come back with no trace of it (2026-11-07)
- **Found:** by the Roxby scout of 7 Nov 2026.
  - Reader R: `2026_Natural_Source_IP\datasets\roxby\results\scout_20261107\report_readers.md`, package candidate A1; `tables\reader_trial.csv`, column clock_error; `logs\reader.log`, the faults run of 13:20:44.
  - Reader H's walk of every TS file (`tables\ts_walk.csv`): clock status 4 on 37,398,554 TS4 records and 3 on 34,584; clock error -4..+3 (TS4), -2..+2 (TS2), -1..+2 (TS3).
  - Filed by the scout's notes pass. mt-io was not re-run for this entry; the observation is reader R's.
- **Reproduction:** mt-io 0.0.5 (bbmt-2026, `C:\Users\joint\anaconda3\envs\bbmt-2026\Lib\site-packages\mt_io`).
  - File: `E:\MT_Timeseries_DATA\MT_Roxby_BHP_2018\171126-27\2070B26A.TS4` (166,930,582 bytes, 73,151 records of 1 s at 150 Hz, box 2070, firmware 3112G3).
  - (1) Own walk of the tags (record = 32-byte tag + 150 scans x 5 channels x 3 bytes; the walk ends exactly at end of file). Clock status (byte 21) is 4 on all 73,151 records. Clock error (bytes 22-25) is non-zero on 176 records: 175 with value 1, 1 with value 3. The same file's TS2 and TS3 have 12 non-zero each. 4262202A.TS4 (59,274 records) has 0.
  - (2) `from mt_io.phoenix.readers import MTUTSN; o = MTUTSN(r"<file>"); o.read(); print(list(o.ts_metadata))`.
  - Expected: the per-record clock status and clock error, as arrays beside the samples or at least as counts.
  - Observed: `ts_metadata` keys `box_number`, `ts_type`, `sample_rate`, `n_ch`, `n_scan`, `start`, `ts_length`, `n_block`, and no per-record array anywhere. The samples themselves are read bit for bit (the scout's R2, 240,069,750 samples on three recordings).
- **Where:** `mt_io/phoenix/readers/mtu/mtu_ts.py`, as 564 names:
  - 282: `_read_header`, `ts_fid.seek(4, 1)` over bytes 14-17 of the first tag;
  - 287: the clock status byte, skipped;
  - 391: `_process_data_block`, `ts_fid.seek(32, 1)` steps over every record's tag, bytes 21-25 included.
- **Effect:**
  - The receiver records per second whether its clock was locked (status) and its estimate of the clock's error. Through mt-io a caller cannot see which seconds of a recording the receiver itself marked as off its time base.
  - On these files the error is small and rare (175 values of 1 and one of 3 in 73,151 records on 2070B26A; 2,796 non-zero in 37,433,138 TS4 records survey-wide). The scout did not establish its unit [inference].
  - The 11 Oct 2026 check of three other Roxby recordings (`2026_IAGA_Div6_Data_Standards\verification\mtu5a_roxby_20261011.md`) saw only 0.
- **Workaround:** the mt-workbench `mtu5a` reader (`src/mt_workbench/mtu5a.py`, workbench 117) reads the clock status and clock error from its own walk of the tags and writes them to the archive's `mtu5a_flags.csv` (`write_flags`), so it does not depend on this. Elsewhere: walk the tags independently (the scout's `scripts\mtu_decode.py`).
- **Ask:** per-record arrays `clock_status` and `clock_error` on the reader, beside `status` and `saturation` (564).
- **Cross-reference:** 564. Its Where already names byte 21 by code reading, and its Ask lists `clock_status`; this entry adds the clock error bytes 22-25 and the measured evidence on Roxby files.

## 566. mt-io 0.0.5 (`uoa.orange.OrangeReader`, `OrangeDataReader.parse_header`): the logger's stamps are read as UTC with no way to name the zone the real-time clock ran on; the Kalgoorlie 2006 boxes ran on Western Standard Time, so every run read through `read_orange` is dated 8 h late (2026-11-07)
- **Found:** stage 1 of the Kalgoorlie LP 2006 track (agent A), building the mt-workbench `orangebox` instrument. Stage 0 showed the logger clocks ran on WST (surveys/kalgoorlie_lp_2006/notes/decisions.md D2: the raw hx and hy lie on Gnangara one-minute data shifted +8 h); stage 1's archives, timed with the zone, lie on Gnangara at lag 0 to +1 min with correlation 0.94-0.99 (`D:\MT_DATA\MT_Kalgoorlie_LP_2006_Workspace\qc\stage1\real_test_gnangara.csv`).
- **Reproduction:** `read_orange(sorted(glob(r"E:\MT_Timeseries_DATA\MT_Kalgoorlie_LP_2006\Kalgoorlie_2006_GH_GB\MT_RawData_Separation_Filtering\Kal01\HFM0-0*.BIN")), station_id="Kal01", ...)` starts the run at 2006-05-02T14:56:00+00:00, the header stamp of HFM0-000.BIN; the record began at 06:56:00 UTC. The run and channel metadata carry the same, and a caller who rebuilds the run on another time axis gets mt_timeseries' "end time of dataset ... does not match metadata end" warning unless it resets every time period.
- **Where:** `OrangeDataReader.parse_header` (`pd.to_datetime(line2, format=STAMP_FORMAT, utc=True)`), `parse_end_stamp` likewise; `OrangeReader` takes no zone keyword.
- **Effect:** an 8 h error in every time stamp of a WST box (any box whose clock was set to local time); spectra and single-run transfer functions are not affected, a remote reference or a stack against another clock is, and so is any comparison with an observatory.
- **Workaround:** mt-workbench reads the header and trailer stamps itself, turns them to UTC with the site's `clock_timezone` (zoneinfo), and rebuilds the run on its own UTC grid (`src/mt_workbench/orangebox.py`, `time_base`, `read_orangebox_run`), resetting the run, channel and station time periods.
- **Ask (mt-io):** a `clock_timezone` keyword (IANA name, default UTC) applied to the header and trailer stamps, with the zone in the run metadata; together with the drift of issue 12.

## 567. mt-io 0.0.5 (`uoa.orange.OrangeReader._find_breaks`): the join check compares each header with the previous file's trailer at 2 s, but the trailer is stamped 1-3 s before the next header while the samples run on; continuous files are refused (Kalgoorlie Kal021: HFM3-040 and HFM3-041 at 3 s and 5 s) (2026-11-07)
- **Found:** stage 1 of the Kalgoorlie LP 2006 track (agent A). Over the 1,078 files of the survey (`D:\MT_DATA\MT_Kalgoorlie_LP_2006_Workspace\qc\stage0\bin_stamps.csv`) each trailer lies 0.8-2.8 s short of its file's samples at the box's rate, and the next header 1-2 s after the trailer ("End: 06:55:52", "File HFM0-040.BIN open for logging 06:55:53" in Kal01's HFM0-RPT.TXT); the samples wait in the 4,096-byte FIFO meanwhile. The header stamps themselves keep one straight line against the record index to 0.3 s rms (0.02-0.05 s on box 1) at every site, the first header (the logging start) and the last (the file logging was stopped in) excepted.
- **Reproduction:** `read_orange` of Kal021's 42 files raises "3 s missing between HFM3-039.BIN and HFM3-040.BIN; 5 s missing between HFM3-040.BIN and HFM3-041.BIN"; HFM3-040.BIN's header lies on the line of HFM3-001..039's headers to 0.23 s, so no sample is missing there.
- **Where:** `_find_breaks` (`step = this.start_time - prev.end_time`, refused above `JOIN_TOLERANCE_S` = 2 s).
- **Effect:** a continuous record is split into runs, here a 40 h run and two of 1 h, and a caller that times each run from its own stamps (first header, last trailer) gets one-hour rates 550-830 ppm off and a gap of about 2.5 s that is not in the data.
- **Workaround:** mt-workbench keeps the reader's rule for the runs it hands it (`orangebox.plan_runs`), times every run from the least-squares line of the deployment's header stamps against the record index (`orangebox.header_rate`), and starts a later run at its header less the header latency the line measures (2.45 s at Kal021), so Kal021's second run follows its first within 0.45 s.
- **Ask (mt-io):** join on the headers: a file continues the previous one when its header lies within the tolerance of the previous header plus the previous file's records at the rate the headers keep (or at the nominal rate, with a wider tolerance); report the trailer offsets as information. Related: 11 (the join check itself), 101 (the partial last file holds one record more than its header count: seen again at all 17 Kalgoorlie deployments whose last file was stopped by 'q', e.g. Kal01 HFM0-041.BIN 26,512 records for a count of 26,511).

## 568. aurora 0.6.2 (`transfer_function.regression`, the covariance of the RME and RME_RR estimates): the error of a band's estimate counts every STFT window as independent whatever the window overlap, so a level processed at 75 % overlap prints errors about 1.8 times smaller than the same data at 25 % with the values unchanged (2026-11-08)
- **Found:** the Kalgoorlie LP 2006 track, stage 3 agent I (`surveys/kalgoorlie_lp_2006/notes/stage3/HANDBACK_agentI.md`; mt-workbench's own record is docs/workbench_issues.md 170). When the band layout moved the 25.6-51.2 s bands from a decimation level processed at 75 % overlap (window 819 s) to one at 25 % (window 205 s), their median phase error over 360 partner and stack product points grew 1.63 times while the values did not move; bands moving between two 75 % levels kept their errors (0.89-0.95). One run decided it: Kal024 rr Kal014 (10 Hz, 69 h) with the long levels set to 25 % overlap (`scripts/process_rr.py --overlap-long 25`; log `D:\MT_DATA\MT_Kalgoorlie_LP_2006_Workspace\logs\run1c\diag_Kal024_rr_Kal014_rr_mb4ol25.log`): the phase errors of the four levels whose window exceeds 600 s rose 1.77, 1.79, 1.82 and 2.03 times, about the square root of the ratio of window counts, and the short levels' errors did not change; no impedance moved beyond noise. The test was stated before it ran (fails if the long levels' errors rise less than 1.3 times).
- **Reproduction:** process any pair twice through mt-workbench's `scripts/process_rr.py`, once with the default (25 % overlap, 75 % on levels whose window lasts over 600 s) and once with `--overlap-long 25`; compare the impedance errors level by level. In aurora alone: the same `ConfigCreator` config with `decimations[k].stft.window.overlap` at 96 and at 32 of 128 samples on the deep levels.
- **Where:** the regression's covariance uses the number of Fourier coefficients in the band (the windows times the harmonics) as the degrees of freedom; overlapped Hann windows share samples, so their coefficients are correlated and the effective count is smaller (about half at 75 % overlap for a Hann taper, by Welch's equivalent degrees of freedom; the measured 1.8 lies between that and the full factor 2).
- **Effect:** every product of every survey processed with mt-workbench's default carries errors above the 600 s window boundary (periods above about 50 s at 10 Hz, 500 s at 1 Hz) that are optimistic by about 1.8; every rule built on those errors (best-of replacements, error-above-bound and few-windows flags, "good from" readings, stack-against-partner tests in units of error) reads the boundary as a step. The WA-MT (1 Nov 2026) and Victoria (3 Nov) notes that the deep-level error bars read optimistic, and that more overlap gave smaller printed errors and no steadier estimate (Victoria F-9, 168 runs), are this.
- **Workaround (mt-workbench, 2026-11-08):** the survey's `processing:` block takes `overlap:` and `overlap_long:` in percent (`Survey.overlap_pct`, `Survey.overlap_pct_long`; `scripts/process_rr.py` reads them under the `--overlap` and `--overlap-long` flags); Kalgoorlie declares `overlap_long: 25` (notes/decisions.md D12), so every level overlaps by 25 % and the errors are consistent across levels. The other surveys keep the default and the caveat.
- **Ask (aurora):** scale the covariance by the equivalent degrees of freedom of the taper and overlap in use (Welch's factor), or report both the window count and the equivalent count in the transfer-function summary so a caller can; at the least, document that the errors assume non-overlapping windows.
- **Measured further (2026-11-08, 10:1x):** the 83 Kalgoorlie sources re-run at 25 % overlap on every level (Run 1d) have long-level printed errors 1.73 times Run 1c's (75 %), the short levels identical, and VALUES that are noisier: the 200-1,000 s phase roughness of the base products 1.60 to 3.55 deg at the median, the spread between a site's partner products at 100-1,000 s 1.70 times larger, 28 products losing one-window periods. So the 75 % overlap carries real information (a Hann taper wastes its edges: Welch's variance 0.75/N at 25 %, 0.53/N at 50 %, 0.48/N at 75 % against non-overlapping windows) and the miscount at 75 % is about 1.4, not 1.8; at 50 % the count and the equivalent degrees of freedom nearly agree (three pairs: printed errors 1.44-1.46 times the 75 % ones, values 1.08-1.26 times rougher). The ask stands: with the factor applied, 75 % would give the steadiest values and honest errors at once.

## 569. mt_metadata 1.0.10 (`timeseries.DataLogger`, `timeseries.Magnetic.sensor`, `timeseries.Electric.positive`/`negative`): no field holds an instrument's persistent identifier (a PIDINST DOI), so a logger's, a coil's or an electrode's registry DOI has nowhere to go in MTH5, EDI or EMTF XML but free text (2026-11-08)
- **Found:** the Kalgoorlie LP 2006 track, stage 3 agent M (`surveys/kalgoorlie_lp_2006/notes/stage3/HANDBACK_agentM.md`), building the request of 8 Nov 2026 that each survey record the AuScope instrument registry DOI (https://pidinst.data.auscope.org.au/, prefix 10.82388) of every instrument used, by site.
- **Where:** `DataLogger` has `id`, `manufacturer`, `model`, `name`, `type`, `firmware.*`, `power_source.*`, `timing_system.*`, `data_storage.*`; a magnetic channel's `sensor` has `id`, `manufacturer`, `model`, `name`, `type`; an electrode (`positive`, `negative`) `id`, `manufacturer`, `type` and its position. None takes a DOI or a typed identifier (the PIDINST schema's identifier with its type), and `Station`/`Survey` have no platform identifier. `id` holds the serial (mt-io's readers write it there; the Orange Box reader's `data_logger.id`), so it cannot carry the DOI too.
- **Effect:** the instrument's registry record cannot be stated in the structured metadata of an archive or a transfer function; a reader of an MTH5, an EDI or an EMTF XML cannot find which registered instrument recorded a station without parsing comments.
- **Workaround (mt-workbench, 2026-11-08):** survey.yaml declares the DOIs (`logger_pid`, `sensor_pid_hx/hy/hz`, `electrode_pid`, `platform_pid`; `mt_workbench.survey.Survey.instrument_pids`); ingest writes them as one run and station comment piece `instrument_registry: logger <doi>, ...`; scripts/process_rr.py writes them into the sidecar, one EDI INFO line per instrument (`mt_workbench.instrument_pid_local_logger=<doi>`) and a sentence of https://doi.org/ links in the EMTF XML's Notes (docs/workbench_issues.md 174).
- **Ask (mt_metadata):** an `identifier` (value and type, e.g. DOI, Handle, URL, following PIDINST's Identifier and AlternateIdentifier) on `DataLogger`, on `Instrument`-based sensors and electrodes, and a platform identifier on `Station` or `Run` (the PIDINST platform record of a deployment); and carry them through the EDI (a `>=DEFINEMEAS`/`>HMEAS`/`>EMEAS` or `>INFO` convention) and EMTF XML writers and readers.

## 570. mt_metadata 1.0.10 (EDI reader of `processing_parameters`; follow-up to 115): a processing-parameter key comes back from an EDI in lower case, besides losing all but its last dotted part, so a key that names a site keeps its letters but not their case (2026-11-08)
- **Found:** the Kalgoorlie LP 2006 track, stage 3 agent M (`tests/instrument_pid_unit.py`, `test_products_carry_pids`): the INFO line `transfer_function.processing_parameters.mt_workbench.instrument_pid_remote_member_Kal014_sensor_hx=10.82388/egmph7x7` written by mt_metadata's own EDI writer reads back through `TF.read` as `instrument_pid_remote_member_kal014_sensor_hx=10.82388/egmph7x7`.
- **Where:** the `>INFO` parse into `transfer_function.processing_parameters` (the same path as 115); the value is kept as written.
- **Effect:** metadata only. A key that carries a name (a station, a stack member) loses its case on a round trip through an EDI, so a merge or a rewrite that reads its sources from EDIs cannot rebuild the name exactly; Z, errors and tipper are untouched.
- **Workaround (mt-workbench):** the keys carry no names: a stacked remote's members are numbered in the key and named in the value (`mt_workbench.instrument_pid_remote_m1_logger=<doi> (Kal014)`, `mt_workbench.products.pid_info_lines`), and every key is written with underscores (115).
- **Ask:** keep the key's case and its full dotted path on read (or document that `processing_parameters` keys are normalised).
